This shall mainstream disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, and systems thinking into all levels of formal and non-formal education, vocational training, and continuing professional development. The Department shall promulgate the necessary implementing rules, technical standards, and performance indicators for the effective operationalization of these instruments, and shall review and update them at least once every three (3) years in light of emerging risks and innovations.

heading: Organizational Structure
text: SEC. 8. Organizational Structure. – The Department shall be composed of a Central Office, Regional Climate Resilience Offices (RCROs), and Local Climate Resilience Offices (LCROs), with such Bureaus, Divisions, Services, and Units as may be necessary for the efficient and effective discharge of its powers and functions. The Department shall be headed by a Secretary who shall be appointed by the President, subject to confirmation by the Commission on Appointments. The Secretary shall have authority and supervision over the entire Department and shall be responsible for the execution of national policies on climate resilience. Under the Office of the Secretary, the following offices and officials shall be established: (a) Office of the Secretary, which shall include: (1) The Undersecretary for Strategic Planning and Policy Development, responsible for the formulation, integration, and updating of the National Climate Resilience Framework, and alignment with national development and climate plans; (2) The Undersecretary for Operations and Incident Management, responsible for overseeing the National Disaster Response Coordination Center, Incident Command System activation, early warning dissemination, and emergency logistics; (3) The Undersecretary for Local Resilience and Performance Oversight, tasked with supervising RCROs and LCROs, and enforcing compliance with performance standards and resilience scorecards; (4) The Undersecretary for Risk Governance and Innovation, tasked with managing resilience instruments, such as the National Risk Register, Digital Twin Systems, and the Innovation Challenge Fund; (5) The Undersecretary for Finance, Administration, and Resilience Procurement, who shall manage the Department’s budget, human resources, and compliance with the Resilience Procurement Framework; (6) The Undersecretary for Public Engagement and Education, who shall lead partnerships with DepEd, CHED, TESDA, and civil society on resilience education, advocacy, and inclusion. (b) National Disaster Response Coordination Center (NDRCC) – The NDRCC shall serve as the principal operations center of the Department and shall be activated during emergencies to coordinate inter-agency response under the Incident Command System. (c) Functional Bureaus and Clusters – The Department shall be composed of the following core bureaus and clusters, each headed by a Bureau Director, and organized to reflect the full disaster risk management and resilience continuum, with powers, functions, and internal units to be defined in the Implementing Rules and Regulations:: (1) Bureau of Risk Governance and Planning – Shall lead the development and periodic updating of the National Climate Resilience Framework (NCRF), conduct integrated risk and resilience assessments, hazard and scenario modeling, and ensure the mainstreaming of risk-informed decision-making in national and local development plans, investment programs, land use plans, and regulatory processes. (2) Bureau of Preparedness and Early Action – Shall develop anticipatory governance protocols, operationalize early warning and early action systems, oversee inter-agency contingency planning, and coordinate community readiness campaigns, including drills, civil protection advisories, and simulation exercises. (3) Bureau of Response Coordination and Emergency Operations – Shall operate and manage the National Emergency Operations Center (NEOC) under an Incident Command System (ICS), coordinate multi-agency disaster response, mobilize national and international assets, and provide surge technical support and deployment to affected LGUs during emergencies. (4) Bureau of Recovery and Resilient Rehabilitation – Shall lead pre-disaster recovery planning (PDRP), implement post-disaster needs assessments (PDNA), coordinate the formulation and financing of recovery and rehabilitation programs, and ensure alignment with resilience and sustainable development principles. (5) Bureau of Resilience Financing and Innovation – Shall manage the National Resilience Fund, resilience bonds, risk transfer and insurance instruments, and oversee the Resilience Innovation Challenge Fund; institutionalize resilience procurement systems and support risk-informed budget tagging, resource mobilization, and fiscal planning. (6) Bureau of Capacity Development and Local Empowerment – Shall design, accredit, and deliver training and certification programs for DRRM professionals and LDRO staff; strengthen technical and operational capacities of LGUs; support the establishment and operation of Localized Resilience Hubs; and promote convergence with DILG, CSC, CHED, TESDA, and development partners. (7) Bureau of Resilience Justice, Inclusion, and Education – Shall mainstream rights-based and inclusive DRRM approaches across Department programs, ensure participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups, oversee grievance and accountability mechanisms, and lead the implementation of resilience education strategies in collaboration with DepEd, CHED, and civil society actors. (8) Cluster for Science, Digital, and Climate Systems – Shall serve as the Department’s technical arm on scientific modeling, digital twin systems, climate analytics, and the integration of geospatial data, remote sensing, and emerging technologies in support of real-time risk governance and early decision-making systems. (d) Regional Offices – The Department shall establish a Regional Climate Resilience Office (RCRO) in each administrative region, headed by a Regional Director. The RDRO shall coordinate with Regional Development Councils, Regional DRRM Councils, and provincial governments in implementing the Department’s programs and providing technical assistance. (e) Local Climate Resilience Support Units – Each province and highly urbanized city shall be supported by a Local Climate Resilience Support Unit, which shall serve as the Department’s operating arm in facilitating program delivery, institutional development of Local Climate Resilience Offices, and coordination of Resilience Hubs. (f) Advisory and Technical Bodies – The Department shall constitute the following advisory and technical bodies: (1) National Scientific and Technical Advisory Panel on Resilience – Composed of scientists, researchers, and innovation experts from the public and private sectors, tasked to provide strategic guidance, review technical standards, and ensure science-based decision-making. (2) Multi-Sectoral Resilience Council – A permanent consultative body composed of representatives from national government agencies, LGUs, civil society, academe, private sector, and affected communities to advise on the design, implementation, and evaluation of the Department’s programs. (g) Professionalization and Technical Staffing – The Department shall establish a career service system for climate resilience professionals, technical specialists, and support personnel. All personnel involved in disaster risk reduction and resilience functions shall undergo continuous professional development, certification, and ethical training under standards prescribed by the Department in consultation with the Civil Service Commission. (h) Attachment of Existing Institutions – The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and relevant units of the Department of National Defense, including the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council Secretariat, shall be absorbed into the Department as integral components of the new structure. The integration shall ensure continuity of operations and retention of qualified personnel, subject to civil service rules.

heading: Local Implementation and Support Mechanisms
text: SEC. 9. Local Implementation and Support Mechanisms. – The Department shall institutionalize the following mechanisms and structures to ensure the operationalization of climate resilience policies and programs at the subnational and community levels: (a) Local Climate Resilience Offices (LCROs) – Each province, city, and municipality shall establish and maintain a Local Climate Resilience Office (LCRO), to be headed by a duly appointed Local Climate Resilience Officer (LCR Officer), with a permanent plantilla and appropriate qualifications, in accordance with standards prescribed by the Department, the Civil Service Commission, and the Department of the Interior and Local Government. The LCRO shall be responsible for implementing risk reduction, preparedness, response, recovery, and adaptation programs within its jurisdiction, aligned with the National Climate Resilience Framework and local development plans. It shall coordinate all resilience-related functions of the LGU, and serve as the principal liaison with the Department. (b) Local Resilience Planning and Programming – LGUs shall prepare and implement Local Climate Resilience Plans (LCRPs) integrating multi-hazard risk assessments, climate projections, and socio-economic vulnerability indicators. The LCRPs shall form part of the Comprehensive Development Plan, Comprehensive Land Use Plan, and Annual Investment Plan of the LGU, subject to review and technical guidance by the Department. (c) Localized Resilience Hubs – Provincial and highly urbanized city governments shall establish Localized Resilience Hubs, in coordination with the Department, academic institutions, civil society, and the private sector. These hubs shall serve as centers for: (1) Community-based training and simulation; (2) Knowledge exchange and innovation incubation; (3) Data harmonization and localized early warning systems; (4) Coordination of post-disaster recovery activities and public-private collaboration. (d) Technical and Financial Assistance – The Department shall extend technical assistance, capacity-building programs, seed grants, and performance-based funding to LGUs to enhance local resilience systems. It shall also facilitate LGU access to national resilience financing instruments, subject to compliance with performance benchmarks, planning standards, and audit requirements. (e) Oversight and Performance Monitoring – The Department shall monitor the performance of LGUs and LDROs through the Local Resilience Performance Index (LRPI), and shall establish a system of incentives, compliance enforcement, and capacity interventions based on annual performance ratings. Results shall be published and used to inform national resource allocation.

heading: Inter-Agency and Multisectoral Coordination
text: SEC. 10. Inter-Agency and Multisectoral Coordination. – The Department shall institutionalize inter-agency, intergovernmental, and multisectoral coordination systems as follows: (a) National Climate Resilience Council (NCRC) – There is hereby created a National Climate Resilience Council (NCRC), chaired by the Secretary of the Department, with the following as members, who shall provide high-level policy direction, and ensure alignment and accountability in the implementation of the NCRF, and other national policies and programs: (1) the Secretary of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG); (2) the Secretary of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD); (3) the Secretary of the Department of National Defense (DND); (4) the Secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR); (5) the Secretary of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST); (6) the Secretary of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH); (7) the Secretary of the Department of Health (DOH); (8) the Secretary of the Department of Agriculture (DA); (9) the Secretary of the Department of Finance (DOF); (10)        the Secretary of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM); (11)        the Secretary of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT); (12)        the Chairperson of the Climate Change Commission; the Administrator of the Office of Civil Defense (OCD); (13)        the Commanding General of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP); (14)        the Chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP); (15)        the Commandant of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG); (16)        the Director of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP); (17)        the President of the League of Provinces of the Philippines; (18)        the President of the League of Cities of the Philippines; (19)        the President of the League of Municipalities of the Philippines; and (20)        representatives from the private sector, civil society, academe, and development partners as may be determined by the Secretary. (b) Regional and Local Coordination Councils – Regional and Local Climate Resilience Councils shall be established, consistent with the structure of the NCRC, and chaired respectively by the Department’s Regional Directors and Local Chief Executives. These councils shall facilitate subnational implementation, joint planning, and harmonized delivery of services and investments for climate resilience. (c) Inter-Cluster Operational Coordination – The Department shall, in coordination with the DSWD, DND, DILG, DOH, DA, DENR, DPWH, AFP, BFP, PNP, PCG, and other relevant government instrumentalities, establish an integrated operational coordination system across preparedness, response, recovery, and rehabilitation functions. The Incident Command System (ICS) shall be the primary structure for field-level coordination and resource mobilization during emergencies. (d) Public-Private Partnerships and Sectoral Engagement – The Department shall institutionalize a mechanism for formal engagement with private sector entities, industry associations, utilities, financial institutions, and media, including through Public-Private Resilience Compacts, Joint Training Protocols, and Shared Infrastructure Audits. Priority shall be given to partnerships that enhance the resilience of critical infrastructure and supply chains. (e) Academic, Scientific, and Civil Society Engagement – The Department shall maintain active collaboration with academic institutions, think tanks, scientific agencies, and civil society organizations, including through the establishment of a National Resilience Knowledge and Innovation Consortium. This body shall support data-driven policy formulation, evidence-based interventions, innovation scaling, and participatory monitoring.

heading: Emergency and Post-Disaster Management
text: SEC. 11. Emergency and Post-Disaster Management.. – The Department shall exercise leadership, supervision, and coordination over all phases of emergency operations and post- disaster management in accordance with the National ClimateResilience Framework (NCRF). It shall ensure the timely, efficient, and accountable delivery of services, deployment of resources, and execution of recovery plans, in coordination with relevant national agencies, local government units, and partner sectors. In the event of a disaster or imminent threat thereof, the Department shall activate the National Emergency Operations Center (NEOC), which shall serve as the unified command center for strategic coordination, operational decision-making, situational analysis, resource tracking, and interagency tasking. The NEOC shall operate in accordance with the Incident Command System (ICS) and national response protocols. To ensure anticipatory and adaptive emergency governance, the Department shall establish the following: (a) National Emergency Operations Center (NEOC). – The Department shall operate and maintain a 24/7 National Emergency Operations Center (NEOC), which shall serve as the central command and control facility for situational monitoring, interagency coordination, decision support, and deployment management during emergencies. The NEOC shall be supported by Regional Emergency Operations Centers (REOCs) and linked to Local Emergency Operations Centers (LEOCs) established by LGUs. (b) Incident Command System (ICS) – This shall be the standardized, scalable, and modular structure for tactical and operational response at the incident level. The Department shall ensure that all national agencies and local government units are trained, certified, and equipped to deploy and operate under ICS protocols. It shall issue harmonized guidelines on chain of command, resource coordination, emergency communications, and field operations integration. (c) Multi-Hazard Contingency and Recovery Planning – The Department shall lead the development, updating, and testing of Multi-Hazard Contingency Plans (MHCPs), Pre-Disaster Recovery Plans (PDRPs), and Emergency Support Functions (ESFs), which shall be aligned with the NCRF and updated based on risk forecasts and seasonal threats. (d) Resource Mobilization and Logistics – This protocol developed by the Department shall include pre-positioning of critical supplies, coordination with humanitarian actors, digital inventory systems, and real-time tracking of deployment. Strategic partnerships with the private sector, military, and international partners shall be pursued to enhance surge capacity and ensure access to remote and underserved areas. (e) Emergency Response Cluster Activation – In coordination with other government agencies, the Department shall activate sector-specific response clusters (e.g., health, shelter, food security, water and sanitation, education, protection, transport, energy, and communications) based on the nature and scope of the emergency. Cluster leads shall be designated in advance and response plans shall be aligned with the National Climate Resilience Framework. (f) Emergency Communications and Information Management – The Department shall establish a unified emergency communications protocol, in collaboration with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), to ensure real-time data sharing, secure information flows, public alerting, and media engagement. This shall include provisions for accessible early warnings, community-level advisories, and counter-disinformation mechanisms. (g) Technical Assistance to Local Government Units – During disaster situations, the Department shall provide direct technical assistance, surge support, and rapid response teams to affected local governments. It shall coordinate and, when necessary, assume command over local operations in cases of widespread disruption, incapacitation, or declared states of calamity, in accordance with constitutional and statutory limits. (h) Recovery and Resilient Rehabilitation – The Department shall lead the conduct of post-disaster needs assessments, the formulation of recovery plans, and the implementation of resilient rehabilitation programs. These shall be aligned with pre-disaster recovery plans, integrate climate and disaster risk reduction measures, and observe the principles of building back better, environmental sustainability, social inclusion, and institutional strengthening. The Department shall monitor the progress of recovery programs, including infrastructure restoration, housing reconstruction, livelihood recovery, psychosocial support, and local systems rehabilitation. All government agencies, instrumentalities, and local government units shall comply with the emergency protocols, recovery plans, and coordination directives issued by the Department in accordance with this Act.

heading: Recovery and Resilient Rehabilitation
text: SEC. 12. Recovery and Resilient Rehabilitation. – The Department shall lead and coordinate national efforts in recovery and resilient rehabilitation following disasters, emergencies, or complex crisis events, ensuring that such efforts are inclusive, risk-informed, and aligned with long-term development and resilience goals. (a) Pre-Disaster Recovery Planning (PDRP) – The Department shall institutionalize PDRP as a mandatory process at the national and local levels. PDRPs shall define sectoral recovery strategies, roles and responsibilities, funding arrangements, and implementation timelines prior to the occurrence of disasters. These plans shall be integrated into Local Climate Resilience Plans and the National Climate Resilience Framework. (b) Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) – The Department shall develop and maintain standardized methodologies and technical protocols for conducting a comprehensive PDNA, in coordination with concerned national agencies, LGUs, and development partners. PDNAs shall assess physical damages, economic losses, social impacts, and recovery needs, serving as the basis for resilient rehabilitation programming and budget allocations. (c) Resilient Rehabilitation Planning – Rehabilitation plans shall prioritize building back better principles, integrating climate and disaster risk reduction measures, nature-based solutions, resilient infrastructure design, and inclusive reconstruction programs. The Department shall ensure that recovery strategies reduce future vulnerabilities and contribute to systemic resilience. (d) Recovery Financing and Risk Transfer – The Department shall manage and coordinate access to domestic and international recovery financing mechanisms, including the National Resilience Fund, resilience bonds, catastrophe risk insurance, and public-private recovery partnerships. Recovery budgets shall be informed by PDNA findings, subject to public disclosure and oversight. (e) Community and Stakeholder Participation – Recovery and rehabilitation efforts shall be designed and implemented with the meaningful participation of affected communities, civil society organizations, vulnerable groups, the private sector, and local governments. Mechanisms for inclusive consultation, grievance redress, and participatory monitoring shall be established. (f) Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning – The Department shall establish a system for monitoring, evaluating, and documenting all recovery and rehabilitation programs to ensure transparency, accountability, and adaptive learning. Evaluation findings shall inform future policy reforms and updates to the National Climate Resilience Framework. (g) Inter-Agency Coordination – The Department shall ensure the effective coordination of line agencies involved in recovery, including but not limited to infrastructure, housing, health, agriculture, social welfare, education, and environment sectors. Sectoral recovery efforts shall be harmonized through joint planning mechanisms and integrated implementation protocols.

heading: Resilience Financing and Resource Mobilization
text: SEC 13. Resilience Financing and Resource Mobilization. – The Department shall establish and oversee a comprehensive, transparent, and accountable resilience financing system that mobilizes, allocates, and sustains resources to support national and local disaster risk reduction, preparedness, response, recovery, and long-term resilience-building initiatives. It shall implement the following capacity development programs and resilience education initiatives that are inclusive, context-sensitive, gender-responsive, and rights-based, with specific provisions for meaningful participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups: (a) National Resilience Fund – There is hereby created a National Resilience Fund, to be administered by the Department, and funded through annual General Appropriations, official development assistance, international grants, private sector contributions, and other lawful sources. The Fund shall finance programs and projects aligned with the National Climate Resilience Framework, including capacity development, early warning systems, resilient infrastructure, innovation initiatives, and post-disaster recovery. (b) Resilience Bonds and Risk Transfer Instruments – The Department shall design, promote, and operationalize resilience bonds, catastrophe-linked instruments, and other risk transfer mechanisms to incentivize pre-disaster risk reduction investments and ensure rapid access to recovery financing. These instruments shall be developed in collaboration with the Department of Finance, the Insurance Commission, and the private financial sector, and may be made available to LGUs and public infrastructure agencies subject to performance criteria. (c) Performance-Based Budgeting – The Department shall develop and implement a performance-based resilience budgeting system, wherein allocations to national agencies and LGUs shall be guided by their compliance with risk-informed planning standards, Local Resilience Performance Index scores, and implementation track records. The Department shall issue guidelines and monitor adherence in coordination with the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). (d) Resilience Investment Certification – No major public infrastructure or development project shall be approved unless it is certified as climate- and disaster- resilient by the Department, based on multi-hazard risk assessments, sustainability appraisals, and resilience audit protocols. This provision shall apply to projects funded by national government, official development assistance, and public-private partnerships. (e) Public-Private and Multisectoral Financing Partnerships – The Department shall facilitate financing partnerships with private sector institutions, development banks, and philanthropic organizations to co-finance resilience-building efforts, including innovation challenges, digital infrastructure, localized hubs, and green resilience corridors. Incentives such as tax reliefs, co-branding, and streamlined procurement may be authorized through implementing rules. (f) Resource Pooling and Inter-LGU Mechanisms – Subject to appropriate safeguards, the Department shall support the creation of regional or inter-LGU resilience financing mechanisms, such as pooled insurance schemes, joint investment platforms, and mutual aid systems, to address common vulnerabilities and enhance shared capacities. (g) Financial Transparency and Oversight – All resilience funds and financing instruments shall be subject to rigorous transparency and accountability mechanisms, including digital disclosure systems, third-party audits, and citizen monitoring platforms. The Department shall submit an annual Resilience Financing Report to Congress, detailing allocations, disbursements, outcomes, and lessons learned.

heading: Capacity Development, Education, and Innovation for Resilience
text: SEC. 14. Capacity Development, Education, and Innovation for Resilience. – The Department shall lead the formulation, implementation, and monitoring of a comprehensive national strategy for capacity development, education, and innovation that shall support the realization of the National Climate Resilience Framework (NCRF). It shall ensure that knowledge generation, skills upgrading, public awareness, and innovation systems for disaster and climate resilience are institutionalized across all levels of governance and sectors of society. (a) Integration into Formal and Non-Formal Education – In coordination with the Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), and the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), the Department shall integrate disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM), climate change adaptation, systems thinking, and resilience principles into the curricula of basic education, higher education, and technical-vocational training. Inclusive modules shall be developed for early childhood education, indigenous communities, learners with disabilities, and out-of-school youth. (b) Lifelong Learning, Community Preparedness, and Public Engagement – The Department shall institutionalize nationwide capacity-building programs and community-based training initiatives, including but not limited to: mandatory multi-hazard drills, risk communication campaigns, civil protection exercises, and community contingency planning. These shall be coordinated with Local Climate Resilience Offices (LDROs), civil society organizations, and grassroots institutions. Special learning tracks shall be established for youth leaders, community volunteers, and indigenous knowledge holders to support localized leadership in resilience building. (c) Professionalization and Certification of DRRM Personnel – In partnership with the Civil Service Commission (CSC), Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), CHED, and TESDA, the Department shall design and implement a national certification system for climate resilience professionals, technical staff, and volunteers. The system shall include competency standards, accreditation procedures, continuing education mechanisms, and a digital registry of certified practitioners. The Department shall operate a digital training platform accessible to all localities, including geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, to ensure equal learning opportunities. (d) National Resilience Research, Innovation, and Knowledge Hub – The Department shall establish a National Resilience Innovation and Knowledge Hub, which shall serve as a centralized repository of research outputs, good practices, innovation models, and policy-relevant studies on disaster risk and resilience. The Hub shall coordinate applied research partnerships with the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), higher education institutions, development partners, and private innovators. (e) Resilience Innovation Challenge Fund – The Department shall operationalize and manage the Resilience Innovation Challenge Fund, which shall support annual national and local competitions for scalable, locally designed, and data-informed innovations in disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, resilient livelihoods, and inclusive preparedness. Priority shall be given to solutions led by youth, women, persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples, and grassroots innovators. (f) Science-Policy Integration and Technical Exchange – The Department shall establish science-policy interface mechanisms to ensure the continuous translation of scientific research into evidence-based policy, planning, and operational protocols. It shall convene multi-stakeholder technical working groups, facilitate international knowledge exchange, and adopt best practices from global resilience leadership experiences. Data-sharing partnerships shall be established with scientific agencies, including DOST, PAGASA, PHIVOLCS, and NAMRIA. (g) Monitoring of Training Impact and Learning Outcomes – The Department shall design metrics and evaluation tools to assess the effectiveness of training programs, knowledge systems, and innovation initiatives. Training impact shall be assessed using key performance indicators linked to the Local Resilience Performance Index (LRPI) and used to guide future budget allocations, certification renewals, and policy enhancements. ARTICLE III FINAL PROVISIONS

heading: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Accountability for Resilience
text: SEC. 15. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Accountability for Resilience. – The Department shall establish and institutionalize a national system of monitoring, evaluation, and accountability for climate resilience, anchored on the National Climate Resilience Framework (NCRF) and guided by principles of transparency, performance-based governance, and continuous improvement, such as the following: (a) National Resilience Monitoring and Evaluation System – The Department shall develop and institutionalize a National Resilience Monitoring and Evaluation System (NRMES), which shall measure, track, and report on progress in risk reduction, preparedness, early action, response effectiveness, recovery quality, and long-term resilience outcomes. The NRMES shall be data-driven, results-oriented, interoperable with other government information systems, and capable of disaggregating data by location, sector, gender, age, disability, and socioeconomic status. (b) Local Resilience Performance Index (LRPI) – In coordination with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the Department shall implement the Local Resilience Performance Index (LRPI) as a standardized evaluation tool for all provinces, cities, and municipalities. The LRPI shall assess LGU performance in planning, financing, implementing, and institutionalizing DRRM and climate adaptation programs, with results to be published annually. Performance shall be linked to eligibility for access to national resilience funds, technical assistance, and program incentives. (c) National Climate Resilience Scorecard – The Department shall maintain and publicly disclose an annual National Climate Resilience Scorecard, which shall synthesize the country’s overall resilience status based on indicators aligned with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and other international commitments. The Scorecard shall include sectoral performance (e.g., health, infrastructure, education), institutional effectiveness, community resilience metrics, and critical infrastructure resilience. (d) Compliance, Audit, and Enforcement Mechanisms – The Department shall establish and operationalize compliance protocols and audit systems to ensure adherence to resilience standards, procurement guidelines, risk-informed planning mandates, and emergency response protocols by national agencies, LGUs, and private sector entities involved in resilience programs. It shall conduct regular field audits, independent evaluations, and third-party verifications, and may recommend the withholding of funds or referral to appropriate authorities for violations, gross negligence, or willful non-compliance. (e) Citizen Feedback, Grievance Redress, and Participatory Monitoring – A national grievance redress and citizen feedback mechanism shall be instituted to allow individuals, communities, and civil society organizations to report deficiencies, suggest improvements, or file complaints concerning resilience programs, projects, and disaster response actions. The Department shall ensure that mechanisms are accessible, inclusive, and responsive, and that they inform adaptive changes in policies and programs. (f) Transparency, Open Data, and Public Accountability – All performance data, audit results, resilience scores, risk maps, and investment tracking reports generated by the Department shall be made publicly accessible through a digital transparency portal. The portal shall include open data dashboards, geospatial risk overlays, real- time disaster response tracking, and summary reports to ensure public accountability and informed decision-making by all stakeholders. (g) Periodic Independent Review – An independent multi-sectoral commission composed of representatives from the academe, civil society, the private sector, and international partners shall be convened at least once every three (3) years to conduct an external review of the Department’s effectiveness, institutional integrity, and contribution to national resilience. Recommendations of the review commission shall be submitted to Congress, the Office of the President, and made available to the public. The Department shall issue detailed guidelines, indicators, reporting protocols, and accountability standards to implement this Section, in coordination with oversight bodies including the Commission on Audit (COA), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), and the Civil Service Commission (CSC).

heading: Resilience Research, Foresight, and Knowledge Management
text: SEC. 16. Resilience Research, Foresight, and Knowledge Management. – To advance science-based, anticipatory, and adaptive resilience governance, the Department shall establish and institutionalize a national system for resilience-oriented research, foresight, and knowledge integration, establishing the following strategies: (a) The Department shall establish a dedicated Center for Climate Resilience Research and Innovation, which shall serve as the lead implementing and coordinating body for resilience-related research, pilot testing of technologies, local innovation programs, and knowledge dissemination. The Center shall facilitate collaborative projects with universities, local government units, scientific institutions, civil society organizations, and private sector partners, and shall support the translation of research into actionable policies and local solutions. (b) The Department, through the Center for Climate Resilience Research and Innovation, shall develop and implement a rolling five-year National Resilience Research and Innovation Agenda in coordination with the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), academic institutions, and international knowledge networks. The Agenda shall prioritize the following areas: (1) Hazard mapping, scenario modeling, and impact forecasting using emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), remote sensing, and high-performance computing; (2) Locally adapted climate and disaster risk reduction technologies and indigenous knowledge systems; (3) Nature-based solutions and green infrastructure for disaster mitigation and adaptation; (4) Resilient infrastructure design, retrofitting methods, and materials science; (5) Community-based risk governance, social protection models, and equity- centered approaches; (6) Behavioral and systems science for early warning uptake, preparedness, and recovery; (7) Innovation in financial instruments and insurance models for risk transfer. (c) The Department shall develop and maintain a centralized and interoperable Resilience Knowledge Platform to serve as a public repository of resilience data, research findings, learning modules, analytics tools, and best practices. The Platform shall promote open access, enable evidence-based policymaking, and support local governments, civil society, and the private sector in enhancing risk governance capacities. (d) The Department shall establish and administer a Resilience Innovation Challenge Fund, which shall provide grants, technical support, and incubation assistance to research institutions, startups, social enterprises, and grassroots innovators pursuing solution-driven initiatives aligned with the National Climate Resilience Framework. The Fund shall prioritize high-impact innovations capable of local implementation and scalable adaptation. (e) A distinct technical unit within the Department shall be designated or created as the Center for Resilience Futures and Strategic Foresight. It shall conduct scenario planning, long-term systems modeling, risk horizon scanning, and simulation- based policy testing to inform anticipatory governance. The Center shall work in collaboration with international foresight institutions and local research groups. (f) The Department shall ensure that resilience-related research outputs, innovations, and knowledge products are converted into practical guidance materials, toolkits, planning aids, and operational templates for use by LGUs, local communities, and institutions. Emphasis shall be placed on usability, gender-sensitivity, cultural appropriateness, and support for marginalized sectors.

heading: Resilience Data Governance and Digital Infrastructure
text: SEC. 17. Resilience Data Governance and Digital Infrastructure. – The Department shall develop and implement a comprehensive Resilience Data Governance Framework, and invest in modern digital infrastructure in coordination with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA), and relevant government agencies. It shall lead the following initiatives: (a) National Resilience Data Ecosystem – The Department shall lead the establishment of an integrated, interoperable, and secure National Resilience Data Ecosystem that shall consolidate multi-hazard risk assessments, vulnerability data, exposure mapping, early warning indicators, infrastructure audits, and real-time disaster analytics. The Ecosystem shall be standardized, geospatially enabled, and capable of disaggregation by gender, age, disability, income, and location to support inclusive, evidence-based decision-making. (b) Resilience Digital Twin Platform – The Department shall develop and operationalize a Resilience Digital Twin Platform—an advanced simulation environment replicating physical, environmental, and socioeconomic systems of the country. The Platform shall support predictive modeling, disaster scenario testing, recovery planning, infrastructure stress simulations, and optimization of preparedness and mitigation investments at both national and local levels. (c) Data Standards, Sharing, and Privacy – The Department shall prescribe national data standards for resilience and risk governance, in consultation with relevant agencies and stakeholders. It shall issue protocols for secure data sharing, protection of personal and sensitive information, and interagency interoperability. All data collected and generated through Department programs shall comply with the provisions of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and other applicable laws. (d) Local Government Digital Enablement – The Department shall support LGUs in adopting and upgrading their own local risk databases, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), emergency operations digital tools, and cloud-based contingency and recovery planning systems. It shall provide technical assistance and capacity building to ensure that digital governance tools are usable, maintained, and integrated into local development planning processes. (e) Open Data and Public Access – The Department shall maintain a publicly accessible Resilience Open Data Portal which shall house non-sensitive data on hazards, risks, disaster impacts, resilience programs, infrastructure vulnerabilities, financing allocations, and real-time updates. This shall promote transparency, academic research, community engagement, and private sector participation in resilience-building efforts.

heading: Congressional Oversight and Public Transparency
text: SEC. 18. Congressional Oversight and Public Transparency. – To ensure institutional accountability, performance integrity, and continued alignment with the national interest, the Department shall be subject to robust congressional oversight and public transparency mechanisms, such as: (a) Congressional Oversight Committee – A Joint Congressional Oversight Committee on Climate Resilience shall be constituted, composed of five (5) Members each from the Senate and the House of Representatives, with representation from the majority and minority. The committee shall monitor the implementation of this Act, assess Department performance, review the NCRF and major policies, and recommend legislative or budgetary amendments as needed. (b) Annual State of Climate Resilience Report – The Secretary of the Department shall submit to the President and Congress an Annual State of Climate Resilience Report, which shall include an integrated assessment of national and local resilience conditions, implementation progress, risk trends, major programs and expenditures, research outcomes, and the National Climate Resilience Scorecard. The report shall be published and made accessible to the public through the Department’s website and the Resilience Knowledge Platform. (c) Public Access and Transparency Measures – The Department shall ensure full disclosure of resilience-related procurement, project implementation status, risk financing utilization, audit reports, and resilience performance data. A Transparency and Accountability Dashboard shall be maintained on its website, linked to the Open Data Portal and integrated with relevant platforms such as the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) and the Commission on Audit (COA). (d) Civil Society and Citizen Participation – The Department shall establish participatory monitoring mechanisms involving civil society organizations, academic institutions, local resilience councils, and grassroots representatives in the assessment of resilience program effectiveness. Regular citizen forums, resilience scorecard consultations, and grievance redress system reviews shall be institutionalized.

heading: Penal Provisions
text: SEC. 19. Penal Provisions. – Any person, whether natural or juridical, including public officials, private contractors, or implementing partners, who commits any of the following acts in violation of this Act shall be held administratively, civilly, and criminally liable, without prejudice to other applicable laws: (a) Gross Negligence or Willful Non-Compliance – Any officer or employee of a government agency, local government unit, or private entity involved in the implementation of this Act who knowingly, deliberately, or with gross negligence fails to observe mandatory risk reduction, preparedness, response, or recovery standards; refuses to comply with lawful directives of the Department; or obstructs the implementation of approved resilience programs shall be liable for administrative sanctions including suspension, dismissal from service, forfeiture of benefits, and disqualification from public office, as appropriate under the Civil Service Law and other applicable rules. (b) Misuse of Resilience Funds – Any person who misappropriates, misuses, or diverts funds allocated for disaster risk reduction, emergency response, resilience building, or post-disaster recovery under this Act, whether from public or authorized private sources, shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than six (6) years but not more than twelve (12) years, and a fine equivalent to double the amount misused, without prejudice to the imposition of perpetual disqualification from holding public office or from participation in any government procurement program. (c) Falsification, Obstruction, or Manipulation of Data – Any person who falsifies, conceals, or deliberately manipulates risk data, resilience scorecards, monitoring reports, infrastructure vulnerability assessments, or audit findings, or obstructs authorized data collection and transparency mechanisms, shall be penalized with imprisonment of not less than four (4) years but not more than ten (10) years, and a fine not less than Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (₱500,000), in addition to administrative liability, if applicable. (d) Failure to Implement Mandatory Evacuation or Early Warning Protocols – Any responsible official who, without justifiable cause, fails to issue or enforce mandatory evacuation orders, early warnings, or other urgent protective measures, resulting in loss of life or serious injury, shall be criminally and administratively liable under relevant laws and the provisions of this Act. (e) Violation of Risk-Informed Procurement and Infrastructure Standards – Any individual or entity that knowingly violates procurement standards, building codes, or critical infrastructure resilience requirements prescribed by the Department shall be subject to administrative and civil liability, and may be barred from participating in future resilience or recovery-related projects for a period not less than five (5) years. (f) Obstruction of Emergency Operations – Any person who impedes or obstructs duly authorized emergency response operations, including the mobilization of supplies, personnel, equipment, or access to disaster sites, shall be liable for penalties under this Act and other applicable laws, including but not limited to those governing obstruction of justice, sabotage, and interference with lawful authority. The imposition of the above penalties shall be without prejudice to prosecution under the Revised Penal Code, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, the Government Procurement Reform Act, the Anti-Red Tape Act, and other special penal laws, when such acts constitute distinct offenses.

heading: Appropriations
text: SEC. 20. Appropriations. – The amount necessary for the initial implementation of this Act shall be charged against the current year’s available appropriations of agencies whose functions are herein absorbed, transferred, or realigned to the Department of Climate Resilience. Thereafter, such sums as may be necessary for the continued implementation of this Act shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act. To ensure sufficient and sustained financial capacity, the Department shall be prioritized in the allocation of national government resources for resilience-building, emergency preparedness, response capability enhancement, and post-disaster recovery. The Department is hereby authorized to receive, manage, and utilize grants, donations, loans, and other official development assistance, domestic or foreign, subject to existing budgetary, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations. The appropriations shall cover funding for: (a) The establishment and operation of the central, regional, and local offices of the Department; (b) The development and implementation of the National Climate Resilience Framework (NCRF), Integrated Planning and Governance Instruments, and resilience innovation programs; (c) The maintenance of the National Emergency Operations Center and affiliated Regional and Local Emergency Operations Centers; (d) The capitalization of the Resilience Innovation Challenge Fund, Resilience Bonds, and other resilience financing mechanisms; (e) Human resources, systems development, digital infrastructure, and capacity- building initiatives; (f) Pre-positioned logistical hubs, early warning technologies, and rapid response assets; and (g) All other activities necessary to fulfill the Department’s mandate under this Act.

heading: Implementing Rules and Regulations
text: SEC. 21. Implementing Rules and Regulations. – Within ninety (90) days from the effectivity of this Act, the Department of Climate Resilience, in coordination with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), and other relevant agencies, shall promulgate the necessary rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act. The Implementing Rules and Regulations shall be developed through a consultative process involving local government units, civil society organizations, the private sector, academic institutions, and other stakeholders.

heading: Separability Clause
text: SEC. 22. Separability Clause. – If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional or invalid, the remaining provisions not affected shall continue to be in full force and effect.

heading: Repealing Clause
text: SEC. 23. Repealing Clause. – All laws, decrees, executive orders, rules and regulations, or parts thereof which are inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed, amended, or modified accordingly.

heading: Effectivity
text: SEC. 24. Effectivity. – This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation. Approved.

heading: Short Title
text: SECTION 1. Short Title - This Act shall be known as the “Department of Tertiary Education of 2025”.

heading: Declaration of Policy
text: SEC 2. Declaration of Policy - It is the policy of the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels. The State shall take appropriate measures to ensure that education, including tertiary education, is accessible to all. Tertiary education aims to deepen knowledge, develop specialized skills, foster critical thinking, and prepare individuals for professional careers or advanced academic pursuits following the completion of secondary education. The State further commits to encouraging and supporting non-formal, informal, and Indigenous learning systems, as well as_ self-learning, independent, and out-of-school study programs, particularly those that address community needs. To this end, the Department of Tertiary Education (“DTE”) shall be established, integrating the functions of the Commission on Higher Education (“CHED”) and the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (“TESDA”) into a single agency for efficient governance, streamlined regulation, and industry-aligned workforce development.

heading: Definition of Terms
text: SEC. 3. Definition of Terms - As used in this Act, the following terms are defined as follows: i. Tertiary Education - The level of formal education that follows secondary education, encompassing undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate studies, as il. iv. vii. viii. well as professional and technical programs that lead to certifications, diplomas, or academic degrees; Department of Tertiary Education (“DTE”) - The primary government agency responsible for regulating, overseeing, and enhancing all post-secondary education institutions, policies, and programs, including higher education, technical and vocational education, and non- traditional learning pathways; Higher Education Institution (“HEI”) - A university, college, or academic institution authorized to offer undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate programs leading to academic degrees. HEIs may be public or private and are subject to accreditation and regulatory standards set by the Department; Technical and Vocational Education and Training (“TVET”) - A structured learning system that provides skills-based education and hands-on training for specific trades, industries, or professions. TVET programs may be delivered through formal institutions, workplace-based learning, or community-based training initiatives; Accreditation - The process of evaluating and certifying the quality and standards of an educational institution, program, or training provider to ensure compliance with regulatory and academic benchmarks; Industry Linkages - Partnerships between educational institutions and businesses to enhance employability and workforce development; Workforce Development - The strategic effort to equip students and graduates with industry-relevant skills, knowledge, and competencies to enhance employability and economic productivity; and Institutional Recognition - The formal authorization granted by the Department to an educational institution, affirming its compliance with academic standards, regulatory requirements, and national education policies.

heading: Creation of the Department of Tertiary Education
text: SEC. 4. Creation of the Department of Tertiary Education - The Department of Tertiary Education, herein referred to as Department, is hereby created as the primary government agency responsible for the regulation, development, and coordination of both higher education and TVET in the country. It shall formulate policies, set academic and competency standards, ensure quality assurance, and provide financial and institutional support to public and private tertiary education institutions. The DTE shall also oversee skills development programs, accreditation of technical-vocational institutions, and workforce alignment to industry needs, fostering a seamless, inclusive, and globally competitive tertiary education system.

heading: Abolition of CHED and TESDA ~ The CHED and TESDA are
text: SEC. 5. Abolition of CHED and TESDA ~ The CHED and TESDA are hereby abolished. Their powers, functions, assets, liabilities, and personnel shall be transferred to the Department of Tertiary Education (DTE), as deemed necessary for its operations, upon its official commencement. ARTICLE I Powers and Functions of the Department

heading: Powers and Functions
text: SEC. 6. Powers and Functions - The Department shall have the following powers and functions: i. Regulatory and Policy Functions: a. Formulate and implement policies, plans, and programs for tertiary education and TVET; b. Set academic, competency, and training standards for universities, colleges, and _ technical-vocational institutions; c. Ensure compliance with quality assurance mechanisms through accreditation, assessment, and monitoring of institutions; d. Establish a unified qualifications framework to standardize academic and technical certifications and facilitate career mobility; and e. Promote lifelong learning and skills development through flexible education pathways and recognition of prior learning. ii. Institutional Development and Support: a. Provide financial assistance and grants to public and private tertiary institutions for capacity building and infrastructure development; b. Oversee licensing and accreditation of HEIs and TVET providers; c. Enhance faculty development programs through scholarships, research grants, and training; d. Support research and innovation by funding projects that contribute to national development, and e. Encourage industry-academe linkages to ensure curricula are aligned with labor market needs. iii | Student Support and Scholarship Programs: a. Administer government-funded scholarship, grant, and financial aid programs for students in higher education and technical-vocational training; Develop and implement a national student loan program to ensure access to quality tertiary education; Provide career guidance and job placement services to facilitate employability of graduates; and Promote inclusive education by supporting disadvantaged and marginalized students, including persons with disabilities (“PWDs”), indigenous peoples (“Ips”), and out-of-school youth. iv. Workforce Development and Industry Collaboration: a. b. Conduct labor market analysis to align educational programs with industry demands; Develop competency-based training programs in coordination with industries and employers; Certify and assess technical-vocational graduates based on industry-recognized competency standards; Promote apprenticeships, on-the-job training (“OJT”), and dual-training programs in partnership with private sector employers; and Facilitate skills retraining and upskilling programs for workforce adaptability in emerging industries. v. Governance and International Cooperation: a. Coordinate with local and international education bodies to ensure global competitiveness of Filipino graduates; Foster internationalization of education through student exchange programs and _ transnational education partnerships; Standardize credit transfer and recognition systems to enable mobility between higher education and technical-vocational training; Develop digital learning and open education resources to expand access to quality tertiary education; and e. Ensure equitable regional distribution of educational opportunities by supporting institutions in underserved areas. ARTICLE II Organizational Structure

heading: Composition
text: SEC. 7. Composition - The Department of shall be composed of the following: i. Office of the Secretary a. Secretary of Tertiary Education - Head of the department, responsible for overall leadership, policy direction, and administration; Undersecretary for Higher Education - Oversees universities, colleges, and other degree-granting institutions; Undersecretary for TVET - Manages technical- vocational institutions and workforce development programs; Undersecretary for Institutional Development and Student Affairs - Handles accreditation, scholarships, and student support programs; and Undersecretary for Industry Collaboration and International Affairs - Focuses on industry linkages, apprenticeships, global partnerships, and educational mobility. ii. heading: Transition Provisions

heading: Title
text: SECTION 1. Title - This Act shall be known as the “Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative Development (BACD) Act of 2025”.

heading: Declaration of Policy
text: SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy - It is hereby declared the policy of the State to promote the development, empowerment, and sustainability of agricultural cooperatives as vital instruments for rural development, poverty alleviation, food security, and inclusive economic growth. The State recognizes that agricultural cooperatives play a key role in empowering farmers, fisherfolk, and agrarian reform beneficiaries by enabling them to access markets, financing, technologies, and support services. In pursuit of this policy, the State shall establish a dedicated and specialized body under the Department of Agriculture to formulate, implement, and coordinate policies and programs for the growth and professionalization of agricultural and agrarian reform cooperatives, without prejudice to the mandate of the Cooperative Development Authority in the registration, regulation, and supervision of all types of cooperatives. This Act seeks to institutionalize the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative Development (BACD) to ensure that the development needs of agricultural cooperatives are efficiently addressed and supported through an integrated approach across all levels of government.

heading: Establishment of the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative
text: SECTION 3. Establishment of the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative Development (BACD)- There is hereby created a new agency to be known as the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative Development (BACD), which shall be attached to the Department of Agriculture for policy coordination and program supervision.

heading: Jurisdiction over Agricultural Cooperatives and Agrarian
text: SECTION 4. Jurisdiction over Agricultural Cooperatives and Agrarian Reform Cooperatives. — All agricultural cooperatives and agrarian reform cooperatives (ARCs) shall remain under the registration and regulatory jurisdiction of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA). The BACD shall assume responsibility for the development, promotion, capacity-building, and support services of these cooperatives.

heading: Powers and Functions
text: SECTION 5. Powers and Functions. — The BACD shall have the following powers and functions: a) Provide technical assistance, capacity-building, and development support services to agricultural cooperatives and agrarian reform cooperatives nationwide; b) Facilitate access to credit, financial services, training, and other resources tailored to the needs of agricultural cooperatives; c) Coordinate with the Department of Agriculture, Department of Agrarian Reform, CDA, local government units, and other agencies to promote integrated rural and agricultural development programs; d) Formulate and implement programs and projects aimed at strengthening the governance, productivity, and competitiveness of agricultural cooperatives; e) Monitor and evaluate the progress and impact of development programs for agricultural cooperatives; f) Collaborate with the Cooperative Development Authority on policies and initiatives to support the growth of agricultural cooperatives; g) Perform other functions necessary for the promotion and sustainable development of agricultural cooperatives.

heading: Organizational Structure
text: SECTION 6. Organizational Structure. — The BACD shall be headed by a Director, who shall be appointed by the Secretary of Agriculture. The Department of Agriculture, in coordination with the Department of Budget and Management, shall define the organizational structure, staffing pattern, and budgetary requirements of the BACD.

heading: Transitory Provisions
text: SECTION 7. Transitory Provisions. — All personnel, records, assets, liabilities, and appropriations related to agriculture and agricultural cooperative under the Cooperative Development Authority shall be transferred to the newly created BACD under the Department of Agriculture. However, registration and regulatory functions shall remain with the CDA.

heading: Appropriation
text: SECTION 8. Appropriation. — The initial funding for the establishment of the BACD shall be charged against the current appropriations of the Department of Agriculture. Thereafter, the BACD shall have its budget incorporated in the Department of Agriculture’s appropriations in the General Appropriation Act (GAA).

heading: Implementing Rules and Regulations
text: SECTION 9. Implementing Rules and Regulations. — The Secretary of Agriculture, in coordination with the Cooperative Development Authority, Department of Agrarian Reform, and other relevant agencies, shall promulgate the necessary rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act within ninety (90) days from its effectivity.

heading: Separability Clause
text: SECTION 10. Separability Clause. — If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional or invalid, the remaining provisions not affected shall remain in full force and effect.

heading: Repealing Clause
text: Section 11. Repealing Clause. — All laws, decrees, executive orders, rules, and regulations inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.

heading: Effectivity
text: Section 12. Effectivity. — This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation. Approved,

heading: Short Title
text: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development Act of 2025.”

heading: Declaration of Policy
text: SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. - It is the policy of the State to promote the growth and development of the agricultural sector while ensuring the development, empowerment, and integration of technological advancements in agricultural cooperatives. Recognizing the vitai roie of cooperatives in rural development, the State commits to provide agricultural cooperatives with the necessary tools, infrastructure, and support to enable them to engage in value-added agricultural activities, such as agro-processing, transportation, logistics, and market integration. This effort is designed to allow farmers to increase their income, participate in both local and global markets, and ultimately contribute to achieving fair and equitable prices for both farmers and consumers.

heading: Creation of the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry
text: SEC. 3. Creation of the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development (BACID). - BACID is hereby established under the Department of Agriculture (DA). BACID shall have a dual mandate: first, to support cooperative development, and second, to drive the modernization of agriculture through agro-processing, logistics development, contract growing, and farm consolidation. BACLD builds upon the functions of the Bureau of Agricultural Cooperatives (BACOD), but expands its focus to include agriculture modernization, and value-added agricultural activities, which are not covered by CDA’s mandate.

heading: Mandates of Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development
text: SEC. 4. Mandates of Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development (BACID). - BACID shall be the primary government agency responsible for the development, empowerment, and modernization of agricultural cooperatives. It shall support cooperatives in their integration into the agricultural industry, fostering sustainable growth, and ensuring market competitiveness.

heading: Powers and Functions of Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry
text: SEC. 5. Powers and Functions of Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development (BACID). - BACID shall have the authority to exercise the following powers and functions: a. Develop and implement comprehensive programs to assist cooperatives in their formation, expansion, and sustainability, including offering training, technical assistance, and financial support to promote the growth of the cooperatives. Facilitate the adoption of innovative technologies and sustainable farming practices through agro-processing, logistics, contract farming, and farm consolidation. Expand cooperative participation in local and global markets, ensuring fair pricing, stable markets, and predictable income streams for farmers. Develop and manage partnerships between cooperatives, agribusinesses, and local government units (LGUs) to improve agricultural productivity and ensure food security. Guide cooperatives to establish and strengthen value-added activities, including processing and product branding, to increase farmer profitability. Implement training programs on cooperative governance, financial management, and market development to enhance cooperative operations. Facilitate contract farming arrangements between cooperatives and agribusinesses, securing stable markets and providing necessary resources and technical support to farmers. Support the clustering and consolidation of small farms through cooperatives to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and increase bargaining power. Facilitate access to loans, grants, and subsidies for cooperatives to modernize infrastructure, including processing plants, storage, and transportation networks. Oversee the comphiance of cooperatives with industry standards and best practices, ensuring environmental sustainability and operational efficiency.

heading: Cooperation Between Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry
text: SEC. 6. Cooperation Between Bureau of Agricultural Cooperative and Industry Development (BACID) and Cooperative Development Authority (CDA). - BACID and CDA shall work together to promote cooperative development and agricultural consolidation. CDA will handle regulation, compliance, and governance, while BACID will focus on modernizing agriculture, including clustering small farms and supporting contract growing.

heading: Organizational Structure and Composition of the Board of Administrators
text: SEC. 7. Organizational Structure and Composition of the Board of Administrators of BACID - The Authority shall be governed by a Board of Administrators consisting of a Chairman and six (6) members to be appointed by the President. The Board consist of the following: a. Chairman. — The Chairman shall serve as the Chief Executive Officer of the Board. The Chairman must have demonstrated leadership and technical expertise in cooperative development, agriculture, public policy, or organizational management. b. Members. -—— The six (6) Members of the Board shall be appointed by the President, upon endorsement or nomination by the relevant agencies or sectors, as follows: ii. One (1) representative from ihe cooperative sector, endorsed by the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA), who has at least five (5) years of experience in managing or advising cooperatives engaged in agriculture, agribusiness, or community development; One (1) representative from the private sector, with background in logistics, agritech, market development, or finance, nominated by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTD; iii. | One (1) representative from the academe, with expertise in rural development, agricultural economics, or cooperative systems, to be nominated by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED); iv. One (1) representative from a national farmers’ or fisherfolk organization, endorsed by the Department of Agriculture (DA); v. One (1) nominee of the Department of Agriculture (DA), preferably with experience in policy implementation or program coordination in agricultural modernization or cooperative clustering; vi. One (1) nominee of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA), with relevant technical, legal, or regulatory background. c. Term. -— All members of the Board shall serve a term of three (3) years, renewable for one (1) additional term, and shall serve in a full-time capacity. To ensure continuity, the initial appointees shall serve staggered terms to be determined by the President. d. Qualifications and Disqualifications. — All members must be of proven integrity, competence, and independence, with no conflict of interest in the performance of their uties. They shall not, during their tenure, engage in any activity or business that may conflict with the mandate of the Board. e. Gender and Regional Representation. — In appointing members to the Board, the President shall ensure, as far as practicable, gender balance and regional representation, particularly from underrepresented or marginalized agricultural communities.

heading: Appropriations
text: SEC. 8. Appropriations. - To carry out the provisions of this Act, an initial appropriation is hereby authorized in the General Appropriations Act (GAA). Subsequent budgets shall be provided based on the Bureau’s needs and performance, as determined by the DA. The Bureau may also seek funding from international organizations, private sector partnerships, and other sources of financial support.

heading: Implementing Rules and Regulations
text: SEC. 9. Implementing Rules and Regulations. - The Department of Agriculture, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, shall issue the necessary rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act within ninety (90) days from its approval.

heading: Repealing Clause
text: SEC. 10. Repealing Clause. - All laws, decrees, executive orders, or parts thereof inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are hereby repealed, amended, or modified accordingly.

heading: Separability Clause
text: SEC. 11. Separability Clause. If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional or invalid by a competent court, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

heading: Effectivity
text: SEC. 12. Effectivity. This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation. Approved,
