All government and non-government agencies receiving financial and technical assistance from the government shall be required to formulate their respective annual agency technical education and training plan. The budget to support such plan shall be subject to review 8 and endorsement by the DTESD to the DBM. The DTESD shall evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of agencies skills development program and schemes to make them conform to the quantitative and qualitative objectives of the national technical education and skills development plan.

heading: Technical Education and Skills Development Committees
text: SEC. 19. Technical Education and Skills Development Committees. - The DTESD shall establish Technical Education and Skills Development Committees at the regional and local levels to coordinate and monitor the delivery of all training activities by the public and private sectors, and recommend policy, program and project. This committee shall likewise serve as the Technical Education and Skills Development Committees of the regional and local development councils. The composition of the Technical Education and Skills Development Committees shall be determined by the Secretary.

heading: Enterprise-Based Training Program
text: SEC. 20. Enterprise-Based Training Program. - The DTESD shall promote Enterprise-Based Training as a major mode of training rather than an employment arrangement and shall see to it that it is not subject to abuse by unscrupulous entities.

heading: Establishment and Administration of National Training Standards
text: SEC. 21. Establishment and Administration of National Training Standards. - There shall be national training standards to be established by DTESD-accredited industry committees. The DTESD shall develop and implement a certification and accreditation program in which private industry groups and trade associations are accredited to conduct approved assessment packages, and the local government units to promote such assessment in their respective areas in accordance with the guidelines set by the DTESD. The Secretary shall determine the occupational trades for mandatory certification. All certificates relating to the national training standards and certification system shall be issued by the DTESD through its Regional and Provincial Offices. In consonance with the PQF, the DTESD shall closely collaborate with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) as regards to the assessment of technicians, master craftsman and technologists.

heading: Administration of Training Programs
text: SEC. 22. Administration of Training Programs. - The DTESD shall design and administer training programs and schemes that will develop the capabilities of public and private institutions to provide quality and cost-effective technical education and skills development and related opportunities. Such training programs and schemes shall include teachers’/trainers’ training in occupational trades and related fields of employment, and value development as an integral component of all technical education and training programs.

heading: Assistance to Employers and Organizations
text: SEC. 23. Assistance to Employers and Organizations. - The DTESD shall assist any employer or organization engaged in technical education and training schemes design to attain its objectives under rules and regulations established by the DTESD for this purpose.

heading: Accreditation and Regulation of TESD Programs
text: SEC. 24. Accreditation and Regulation of TESD Programs. - All TESD shall be duly accredited by the DTESD before it is offered to the public by any public, private entity or non- government organization. Non-compliance with the accreditation requirements of the DTESD shall form part of the bases for the possible suspension or cancellation of the entities’ license to operate issued by competent authorities.

heading: Coordination of All TESD Schemes
text: SEC. 25. Coordination of All TESD Schemes. – In order to integrate the national technical education and skills development efforts, all technical education and skills 9 development schemes as provided for in this Act shall comply with national standards as determined by the DTESD particularly those having to do with competency standards. For this purpose, existing technical education and skills development programs in the Government and in the private sector, specifically those wholly or partly financed with government funds, shall be reported to the DTESD which shall assess and evaluate such programs to ensure their efficiency and effectiveness. Noncompliance with the above-mentioned standards as well as reportorial requirements shall be disqualified from any form of government assistance in the field of technical education and skills development.

heading: Enterprise-Based Partnerships and Linkages
text: SEC. 26. Enterprise-Based Partnerships and Linkages. - The DTESD shall establish effective and efficient institutional arrangements with industry bodies and such other organizations or associations to ensure direct participation of employers and workers in the design and implementation of technical education and skills development schemes, competency standardization and certification; and such other functions in the fulfillment of the DTESD’s objectives.

heading: Inclusive Training Opportunities
text: SEC. 27. Inclusive Training Opportunities. - The DTESD shall likewise design and implement a delivery system for community based technical education and skills development opportunities for the marginalized and disadvantaged sectors of the population, including the beneficiaries of Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) as provided under Republic Act No. 11310 or the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program Act, providing them with new tools of wealth creation and with the capability to take on higher value-added gainful activities; and, to share equitably in productivity gains eventually leading to poverty alleviation and reduction.

heading: Skills Competitions
text: SEC. 28. Skills Competitions. - To promote quality technical education and skills development in the country and with the view of participating in international skills competitions, the DTESD, with the active participation of private industries, shall organize and conduct annual skills competitions. The DTESD shall promulgate the necessary rules and guidelines for the effective and efficient conduct of national skills competitions and for the country’s participation in internationals skills competitions such as ASEAN and World Skills Olympics.

heading: The TESD Development Fund
text: SEC. 29. The TESD Development Fund. - A Technical Education and Skills Development Fund is hereby established, to be managed/administered by the DTESD, the income from which shall be utilized exclusively in awarding of grants and providing assistance to training institutions, industries, local government units for upgrading their capabilities and to develop and implement training and training-related activities. The contribution to the fund shall be the following: a) A one-time lump sum appropriation from the National Government; b) An annual contribution from the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration Fund, the amount of which shall be determined by the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration and based on the study on financing capacity of the OWWA fund; c) Donations, grants, endowments, and other bequests or gifts, and any other income generated by the DTESD. The Secretary shall be the administrator of the fund, and as such, shall formulate the necessary implementing guidelines for the management of the fund, subject to the following: 10 a) Unless otherwise stipulated by the private donor, only earnings of private contributions shall be used; and b) No part of the seed capital of the fund, including earnings, thereof, shall be used to underwrite expenses for the administration of the Fund. The Secretary shall appoint a reputable government-accredited investment institution as fund manager, subject to existing government rules and regulations.

heading: Technical Assistance, Incentives and Scholarship Grants
text: SEC. 30. Technical Assistance, Incentives and Scholarship Grants. - The DTESD shall adopt a system of providing technical assistance, incentives and scholarship grants which shall be designed to encourage public and private sector and clientele participation in technical education and training activities along the priorities identified by the National Development Plan/Agenda.

heading: Placement Centers
text: SEC. 31. Placement Centers. - There shall be established a network of placement centers or PLACERS in all the Provincial/District Offices to cater specifically to the job placement of graduates of TESD institutions. These Centers shall be financed and administered by the DTESD. In coordination with the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), these centers shall be part of the National Employment Service Network of the DOLE.

heading: Separation and Retirement from Service
text: SEC. 32. Separation and Retirement from Service. - Employees who are separated from service within six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act as a result of the abolition/reorganization under the provisions of this Act shall receive separation benefits to which they may be entitled under existing laws, orders and issuances: Provided, that those who are qualified to retire under existing retirement laws shall be allowed to retire and receive retirement benefits to which they may be entitled under applicable laws, orders and issuances.

heading: Transitory Provision
text: SEC. 33. Transitory Provision. – The TESDA Secretariat created under Sections 10- 15 of R.A. 7796 shall comprise the initial manpower complement of the DTESD, Provided, that, no employee shall be terminated by virtue of this transfer. The laws and rules on government reorganization as provided under Republic Act No. 6656, otherwise known as the Reorganization Law, shall govern the transfer and reorganization process of the DTESD. The Personnel of the TESDA shall, in a holdover capacity, continue to perform their respective duties and responsibilities and receive their corresponding salaries and benefits until such time when the organizational structure pattern of the DTESD shall have been approved. Provided, That the preparation and approval of the said new organizational structure and staffing pattern shall, as far as practicable, respect and ensure the security of tenure and seniority rights of affected government employees. Those personnel whose positions are not included in the new staffing pattern or who are not reappointed or who choose to be separated as a result of the reorganization shall be paid their separation or retirement benefits under existing laws.

heading: Appropriations
text: SEC. 34. Appropriations. - The amount needed for the initial implementation of this Act shall be taken from the current fiscal year’s appropriation of TESDA. Thereafter, the amount needed for the operation and maintenance of the DTESD shall be included in the General Appropriations Act.

heading: Implementing Rules and Regulations
text: SEC. 35. Implementing Rules and Regulations. - The DTESD shall issue, within a period of ninety (90) days after the effectivity of this Act, the rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act. 11

heading: Separability Clause
text: SEC. 36. Separability Clause. - If, for any reason, any portion or provision of this Act shall be held unconstitutional or invalid, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.

heading: Repealing Clause
text: SEC. 37. Repealing Clause. - Republic Act No. 7796, otherwise known as the “TESDA Act of 1994,” is hereby repealed. All laws, presidential decrees, executive orders, rules and regulations, issuances or parts thereof which are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are repealed, amended or modified accordingly.

heading: Effectivity
text: SEC. 38. Effectivity. - This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation. Approved, 12

heading: 04jccrfucs. -The objectives of this Act are
text: SEC. 3. 04jccrfucs. -The objectives of this Act are: a) To promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and skills development programs to attain global competitiveness and inclusive growth; b) To focus technical education and skills development on meeting the changing demands for quality manpower particularly in support of the development thrust of the country; c) To encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development progranis; 1 d) To recognize and encourage the complementary roles of public and private institutions, enterprises, local government units (LGUs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) in technical education and skills development; e) To develop the capacities of.stakeholders to participate in the planning and delivery of quality technical education and skills development systems; I) To inculcate desirable values through the development of moral character with emphasis on work ethics, self-discipline, self-reliance and nationalism; g) To strongly support the implementation of the Philippine Qualifications Framework or the PQF Act (Republic Act No.10968), the Ladderized Education Act (Republic Act No.10647) and the Dual Training System Act (Republic Act No. 7686); and other laws, decrees and orders on education; h) To maximize returns to the country's investment in technical education and skills development through an efficient graduates' employment facilitation program within the framework of the national employment service network system; and i)   To support in the poverty alleviation efforts by providing the marginalized and vulnerable segments of the country's population access to income generating technical education and skills development opportunities.

text: SEC. 6. Powers ¢#d Fw#cfrous. -The DTESD shall have the following powers and functions: a) Formulate a roadmap for Philippine TESD and set the general directions for education and training policies and standards that shall be embodied in a National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan OVTESDP); c) Assess, review, harmonize and coordinate all TESD policies and programs to ensure overall consistency and implementation of the national policies; 4 d) Organize and constitute various standing committees, subsidiary groups, or technical working groups for efficient integration, coordination and monitoring of TESD programs at the national, regional, and local levels; Creation and Mandate Of the Departi'i'Ient Of Technical Education ¢#d S*J.//a Deve/apmc#f. - There is hereby created a Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD), which shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating and administrative entity of the government for technical education and skills development (TESD) agenda.

heading: Powers ¢#d F##c/i.o#S
text: SEC. 5. Powers ¢#d F##c/i.o#S. - The Department shall exercise the following powers and functions: a) Formulate a national technical education and skills development program, plans, policies, strategies to promote scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development programs, in coordination and in consultation with national and local stakeholders, local government units (LGUs), and other government agencies; b) To ensure permanence and continuity of technical education and skills development program at par with international standards to attain global competitiveness; c) To recommend to the executive and legislative branches, priorities and grants on technical education and skills development and research; d) Assess, review, harmonize and coordinate all TESD policies and programs to ensure overall consistency and implementation of the national policies; e) Organize and constitute various standing committees, subsidiary groups, or technical working groups for efficient integration, coordination and monitoring of TESD programs at the national, regional, and local levels; I) Enter into, make, execute, perform and carry-out domestic and foreign contracts subject to existing laws, rules and regulations; g) Restructure the entire sub-sector consisting of all institutions and programs involved in the promotion and development of middle-level manpower through upgrading, merger and/or phase-out following a user-led strategy; h) Approve training standards and assessment packages as established and conducted by private industries; i)   To instill necessary values through the development of ethical character with emphasis on work ethics, self-discipline, self-reliance and nationalism; j)   To support the implementation of the philippine Qualifications Framework or the PQF Act (Republic Act No. 10968), the Ladderized Education Act (Republic Act No.10647) and the Dual Training System Act (Republic Act No. 7686); and other laws, decrees and orders on education; k) To maximize returns to the country's investment in technical education and skil]s development through an efficient graduates' employment facilitation program within the framework of the national employment service network system; and I) To support in the poverty alleviation efforts by providing the marginalized and vulnerable segments of the country's population access to income generating technical education and skills development opportunities. in) To promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and skills development programs to attain global competitiveness and inclusive orowth; n) To focus technical education and skills development on meeting the changing demands for quality manpower particularly in support of the development thrust of the country; o) To encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development programs; p) To recognize and encourage the complementary roles of public and private institutions, enterprises, local government units (LGUs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) in technical education and skills development; q) Promulgate such rules and regulations and exercise such other powers and functions as may be necessary to carry out effectively the purpose and objectives of this Act; r) Perform such other functions as may be necessary for its effective operations and for the continued enhancement, growth or development of higher education

heading: SHORT TITLE
text: SECTION 1.         SHORT TITLE. — This Act shall be known as the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) Act of 2024 "

heading: DECLARATION OF POLICY – it is hereby
text: SECTION 2.                DECLARATION OF POLICY – it is hereby a declared the policy of the state to: i. Promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and skills    development     programs   to     attain     international competitiveness. ii. Focus technical education and skills development on meeting the changing demands for quality middle-level manpower; iii. Encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of middle-level manpower development programs; iv. Recognize and encourage the complementary roles of public and private institutions in technical education and skills development and training systems; and v. Instill desirable values through the development of moral character with emphasis on work ethic, self-discipline, self-reliance and nationalism. The state shall provide relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development in support of the development of high-quality Filipino manpower responsive to and in accordance with Philippine development goals and priorities. The state shall encourage active participation of various concerned sectors, public as well as private technical-vocational institutions (TVIs) being direct participants in and immediate beneficiaries of a technically educated and trained workforce, in providing technical education services and training opportunities.

heading: Creation   of   the   Department     of     Technical
text: SECTION 3.            Creation   of   the   Department     of     Technical Education and Skills Development. — There is hereby created a Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD), which shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating and administrative entity of the government for technical education and skills development (TESD) agenda.

heading: MANDATE
text: SECTION 4.             MANDATE - The Department shall exercise the following: a) Formulate a national technical education and skills development program, plans, policies, strategies to promote scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development programs, in coordination and in consultation with national and local stakeholders, local government units (LGUs), and other government agencies; b) To ensure permanence and continuity of technical education and skills development program at par with international standards to attain global competitiveness; c) To recommend to the executive and legislative branches, priorities and grants on technical education and skills development and research; d) Assess, review, harmonize and coordinate all TESD policies and programs to ensure overall consistency and implementation of the national policies; e) Organize and constitute various standing committees, subsidiary groups, or technical working groups for efficient integration, coordination and monitoring of TESD programs at the national, regional, and local levels; f) Enter into, make, execute, perform and carry-out domestic and foreign contracts subject to existing laws, rules and regulations; g) Restructure the entire sub-sector consisting of all institutions and programs involved in the promotion and development of middle-level manpower through upgrading, merger and/or phase-out following a user-led strategy; h) Approve training standards and assessment packages as established and conducted by private industries; i) To instill necessary values through the development of ethical character with emphasis on work ethics, self- discipline, self-reliance and nationalism; j) To support the implementation of the Philippine Qualifications Framework or the PQF Act (Republic Act No. 10968), the ladderized Education Act (Republic Act No. 10647) and the Dual Training System Act (Republic Act No. 7686); and other laws, decrees and orders on education; k) To maximize returns to the country's investment in technical education and skills development through an efficient graduates' employment facilitation program within the framework of the national employment service network system; and l) To support in the poverty alleviation efforts by providing the marginalized and vulnerable segments of the country's population access to income generating technical education and skills development opportunities. m) To promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and skills development programs to attain global competitiveness and inclusive growth; n) To focus technical education and skills development on meeting the changing demands for quality manpower particularly in support of the development thrust of the country; o) To encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development programs; p) To recognize and encourage the complementary roles of public and private institutions, enterprises, local government units (LGUs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) in technical education and skills development; q) Promulgate such rules and regulations and exercise such other powers and functions as may be necessary to carry out effectively the purpose and objectives of this Act; r) Perform such other functions as may be necessary for its effective operations and tor the continued enhancement, growth or development of higher education.

heading: COMPOSITION
text: SECTION 5.         COMPOSITION.       -    The   Department   shall   be composed of the Office of the Secretary, and the various bureaus, services and regional and provincial/district offices. The Office of the Secretary shall house the Office of the Department Secretary, the Offices of the Undersecretaries, the Offices of the Assistant Secretaries, and their immediate support staff.

heading: QUALIFICATIONS AND APPOINTMENT
text: SECTION 6.            QUALIFICATIONS AND APPOINTMENT. - No person shall be appointed Secretary, Undersecretary and Assistant Secretary of the Department unless he or she is a citizen and resident of the Philippines, of good moral character, of proven integrity, and with relevant competence and expertise.

heading: BUREAUS, SERVICES, AND STAFFING
text: SECTION 7.            BUREAUS, SERVICES, AND STAFFING. — The bureaus under the Office of the Secretary of DTESD shall be headed by an Executive     Director    to   be    appointed     by   the   President   upon   the recommendation of the Secretary. The Executive Directors shall have the rank and emoluments of Director V.

heading: TECHNICAL          EDUCATION          AND      TRAINING
text: SECTION 8.           TECHNICAL          EDUCATION          AND      TRAINING CENTERS. - The DTESD shall absorb and enhance existing Technical Education and Training Centers and establish a network of national, regional and local technical education and skills development centers for the purpose of promoting technical education and skills development. This network shall include leading training technology centers, training centers in technical vocational schools, including TESDA- administered and supervised     TVIs,     including    arts   and    trades    schools/colleges   and polytechnic institutes, and all other duly accredited public and private dual system educational institutions.

heading: STRUCTURE AND STAFFING PATTERN
text: SECTION 9.           STRUCTURE AND STAFFING PATTERN. - Subject to the approval of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), the Secretary shall determine the organizational structure and create new divisions or units as may be necessary, and appoint officers and employees of the Department and the Commission hereinafter created in accordance with the civil service laws, rules and regulations. The remuneration structure of the position in the staffing pattern shall strictly conform to Republic Act No. 6758, otherwise known as the Salary Standardization Law, as amended. SEC. 16. Formulation of a Comprehensive Development Plan for Middle Level Manpower. The DTESD shall formulate a comprehensive development plan for middle manpower based on a national employment plan or policies for the optimum allocation, development and utilization of skilled workers for employment entrepreneurship and technology development for economic and social growth. This plan shall be updated periodically and submitted to the President for approval. Thereafter, it shall be the plan for the technical education, training, and certification for the entire country within the framework of the National Development Plan. The DTESD shall direct through its offices to call on public agencies, the private sector and academe to assist in this effort. The comprehensive plan shall provide for a reformed industry-based training program including apprenticeship, dual training system and other similar schemes intended to:

heading: Technical Education and Skills Development
text: SECTION 10.          Technical Education and Skills Development Board. The DTESD shall establish Technical Education and Skills Development board at the regional and local levels to coordinate and monitor the delivery of all training activities by the public and private sectors, and recommend policy, program and project. This board shall likewise serve as the Technical Education and Skills Development Committees of the regional and local development councils. The composition of the Technical Education and Skills Development board shall be determined by the Secretary.

heading: Enterprise-Based    Training   Program
text: SECTION 11.          Enterprise-Based    Training   Program.   -   The DTESD shall promote Enterprise-Based Training as a major mode of training rather than an employment arrangement and shall see to it that it is not subject to abuse by unprincipled entities.

heading: Establishment     and    Administration    of    National
text: SECTION 12.           Establishment     and    Administration    of    National Training Standards Policies & Guidelines - There shall be a national training standard to be established by DTESD-accredited industry board. The DTESD shall develop and implement a certification and accreditation program in which private industry groups and trade associations are accredited to conduct approved assessment packages, and the local government units to promote such assessment in their respective areas in accordance with the guidelines set by the DTESD.

heading: Administration of Training Programs
text: SECTION 13.          Administration of Training Programs. - The DTESD shall design and administer training programs and schemes that will develop the capabilities of public and private institutions to provide quality and cost-effective technical education and skills development and related opportunities. This      training    programs       and     schemes   shall    include teachers'/trainers' training in occupational trades and related fields of employment, and value development as an integral component of all technical education and training programs.

heading: Assistance to Establishments
text: SECTION 14.          Assistance to Establishments - The DTESD shall assist any employer or organization engaged in technical education and training schemes design to attain its objectives under rules and regulations established by the DTESD.

heading: Accreditation     and    Regulation   of        TESD
text: SECTION 15.           Accreditation     and    Regulation   of        TESD Programs. - All TESD shall be duly accredited by the DTESD before it is offered to the public by any public, private entity or non- government organization. Non-compliance with the accreditation requirements of the DTESD shall form part of the bases for the possible suspension or cancellation of the entities' license to operate issued by competent authorities.

heading: Enterprise-Based     Connections
text: SECTION       16.          Enterprise-Based     Connections.     -   The DTESD shall establish effective and efficient institutional arrangements with industry bodies and such other organizations or associations to ensure direct participation of employers and workers in the design and implementation of technical education and skills development schemes, competency standardization and certification; and such other functions in the fulfillment of the DTESD's objectives.

heading: DTESD DEVELOPMENT FUND
text: SECTION 17.        DTESD DEVELOPMENT FUND - A DTESDA Development Fund is hereby established, to be managed/administered by the Secretary, the income from which shall be utilized exclusively in awarding of grants and providing assistance to training institutions, industries, local government units for upgrading their capabilities and to develop and implement training and training-related activities. The contribution to the fund shall be the following: a. one-time lump sum appropriation from the National Government; b. annual contribution from the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration Fund, the amount of which should be part of the study on financing in conjunction with letter (D) of Section 34 of RA7796; c. donations, grants, endowments, and other bequests or gifts, and d. any other income generated by the Agency. The Secretary shall be the administrator of the fund, and as such, shall    formulate   the   necessary   implementing     guidelines   for   the management of the fund.

heading: DTESD BUDGET
text: SECTION 18.        DTESD BUDGET - The amount necessary to finance the initial implementation of this Act shall be charged against the existing appropriations of the National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC) and the Bureau of Technical and Vocational Education (BTVE).

heading: TRANSITORY       PROVISION
text: SECTION 19.       TRANSITORY       PROVISION.     —    The   DTESD Secretariat created under Sections IO- 15 of R.A. 7796 shall comprise the initial manpower complement of the DTESD, Provided, that, no employee shall be terminated by virtue of this transfer. The laws and rules on government reorganization as provided under Republic Act No. 6656, otherwise known as the Reorganization Law, shall govern the transfer and reorganization process of the DTESD. The Personnel of the DTESD shall, in a holdover capacity, continue to perform their respective duties and responsibilities and receive their corresponding salaries and benefits until such time when the organizational structure pattern of the DTESD shall have been approved. Provided, That the preparation and approval of the said new organizational structure and staffing pattern shall, as far as practicable, respect and ensure the security of tenure and seniority rights of affected government employees. Those personnel whose positions are not included in the new staffing pattern or who are not reappointed or who choose to be separated as a result of the reorganization shall be paid their separation or retirement benefits under existing laws.

heading: APPROPRIATIONS
text: SECTION 20.        APPROPRIATIONS. - The amount needed for the initial implementation of this Act shall be taken from the current fiscal year's appropriation of TESDA. Thereafter, the amount needed for the operation and maintenance of the DTESD shall be included in the General Appropriations Act. (GAA). The amount of two billion pesos (₱2,000,000,000.00), or so much thereof as may be necessary, is there hereby appropriated as funding, out of any funds in the National Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to carry into effect the provisions of this Act. The State shall hereby provide a separate authorize operational and organizational funding of five hundred million pesos (₱500,000,000.00) to implement and to maintain the continuity of its mandate. The amount necessary to carry out the purposes of this Act shall be included in the annual budget of implementing agencies in the General Appropriations Act (GAA) of the year following its enactment into law and every year thereafter. The state shall hereby authorize the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development to re-align its appropriations, in the current year of the date of the effectivity of this Act to conform with its mandate and requirements.

heading: PERIODIC REPORTS
text: SECTION 21.         PERIODIC REPORTS - The TESDA shall submit periodic reports on its findings and make recommendations on actions to be taken by Congress and Senate and the appropriate department, and in order to carry out the objectives and mandates of this Act.

heading: AUTOMATIC REVIEW
text: SECTION 22.         AUTOMATIC REVIEW - Every three (3) years after the effectivity of this Act, an independent review panel composed of experts to be appointed by the President shall review the policies and programs in the DTESD and shall make recommendations, based on its findings, to the President and to both Houses of Congress.

heading: REPEALING CLAUSE
text: SECTION 23.          REPEALING CLAUSE - All laws, executive orders, issuances, rules and regulations inconsistent with this Act are hereby amended, repealed or modified accordingly.

heading: SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
text: SECTION 24.          SEPARABILITY CLAUSE - If, for any reason or reasons, any portion or provision of this Act shall be held unconstitutional or invalid, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.

heading: EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
text: SECTION 25.          EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE - This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in any newspaper of general circulation. Approved,

heading: Short Title
text: SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) Act”.

heading: Declaration of Policy
text: SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. – It is hereby declared the policy of the State to provide relevant, accessible, high-quality, and efficient technical education and skills development in support of the development of high-quality Filipino middle-level manpower responsive to and in accordance with Philippine development goals and priorities. The State shall encourage active participation of private technical-vocational institutions (TVIs) and private enterprises, being direct participants in and immediate beneficiaries of a technically educated and trained skilled workforce, in providing technical education services and training opportunities.

heading: Statement of Goals and Objectives
text: SEC. 3. Statement of Goals and Objectives. The goals of the DTESD are as follows: a.   International Competitiveness. - To promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and skills development programs to attain international competitiveness; b.   Quality Middle-Level Manpower. - To focus technical education and skills development on meeting the changing demands for quality middle-level manpower and work environment both in the national and international community; c.   Scientific and Technical Knowledge Base. - To encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of middle-level manpower development, training, and programs; d.   Role of Public and Private Institutions. - To recognize and encourage the complementary role of public and private institutions in technical education and skills development and training systems; and Page 3 of 15 e.    Desirable Values. - To inculcate desirable values through the development of moral character, with emphasis on work ethics of honesty, integrity and punctuality, self- discipline, self-reliance, and nationalism. The objectives of the DTESD are: a.    Promotion and strengthening of the quality of technical education and skills development training and programs to attain global competitiveness and spur economic growth; b.    Focus on technical education and skills development to meet the changing demands for quality manpower globally as well as the changing work environment; c.     Encouragement of critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development, training, and programs; d.    Recognition and encouragement of the complementary roles of public and private institutions, enterprises, local government units (LGUs), and civil society organizations (CSOs) in technical education and skills development; e.    Development of the capacities of stakeholders to participate in the planning and delivery of quality technical education and skills development systems; f.    Inculcating desirable values through the development of moral character, with emphasis on work ethics of honesty, integrity and punctuality, self-discipline, self-reliance, and nationalism; g.    Strong support to the implementation of the Philippine Qualification Framework Act (R.A. 10968), the Ladderized Education Program (R.A. 10647) and the Dual Training System (R.A. 7686) and other pertinent laws, decrees, and orders on education; h.    Maximizing returns to the country’s investment in technical education and skills development through an efficient graduates’ employment-facilitation program within the framework of the national employment service network system; and i.    Supporting the poverty alleviation efforts of the government by providing the marginalized and vulnerable segments of the country’s population access to income- generating technical education and skills development opportunities.

heading: Definition of Terms
text: SEC. 4. Definition of Terms. – As used in this Act: a.    Apprenticeship refers to on-the-job practical training with compulsory related theoretical instructions involving a contract between an apprentice and an employer on an approved apprenticeable occupation. b.    Apprentice refers to a person undergoing training for an approved apprenticeable occupation during an apprenticeship agreement; c.    Apprenticeship Agreement refers to a contract wherein a prospective employer binds himself to train the apprentice who in turn accepts the terms of training for a recognized apprenticeable occupation emphasizing the rights, duties, and responsibilities of each Page 4 of 15 party. d.   Apprenticeable Occupation refers to an occupation officially endorsed by a tripartite body and approved as apprenticeable by the Department. e.   Dual Training System refers to an instructional delivery system of technical and vocational education and training that combines in-plant training and in-school training based on a training plan collaboratively designed and implemented by an accredited dual system educational institution/training center and accredited dual system agricultural, industrial and business establishments with prior notice and advice to the local government unit concerned. Under this system, said establishments and the educational institution share the responsibility of providing the trainee with the best possible job qualifications, the former essentially through practical training and the latter by securing an adequate level of specific, general, and occupation-related theoretical instruction. The word “dual” refers to the two parties providing instruction: the concept “system” means that the two instructing parties do not operate independently of one another, but rather coordinate their efforts. f.   Ladderized education refers to the harmonization of all education and training mechanisms that allow students and workers to progress between technical vocational and higher education programs, or vice-versa. It opens opportunities for career and educational advancement to students and workers. It creates a seamless and borderless education and training system that will allow transfers in terms of flexible entry and exit between technical-vocational and higher education programs in the post- secondary school educational system. g.   Leading Technology Center refers to centers that provide high-quality and efficient technical education, training, and certification in support of the development of high- quality Filipino manpower responsive to and in accordance with Philippine development goals and priorities. h.   Learner refers to persons hired as trainees in semi-skilled and other industrial occupations that are non-apprenticeable. Learnership programs must be approved by the Department. i.   Levy Grant System refers to a legal contribution from participating employers who would be beneficiaries of the program (often as a percentage of the payroll) which is subsequently turned over or rebated to enterprises offering employee training programs. j.   Middle-Level Manpower refers to those: i)    Who have acquired practical skills and knowledge through formal or non- formal education and training equivalent to at least a secondary education but preferably at post-secondary education with a corresponding degree or diploma; or ii)   Skilled workers who have become highly competent in their trade or craft as attested by the industry. iii) Philippine Qualifications Framework (PQF) refers to the national policy that Page 5 of 15 describes the levels of educational qualifications and sets the standards for qualification outcomes. It is a quality-assured national system for the development, recognition, and award of qualifications based on standards of knowledge, skills, and values acquired in different ways and methods by learners and workers of a certain country. iv) Private Enterprise refers to an economic system under which property of all kinds can be privately owned and in which individuals, alone or in association with others, can embark on a business activity. This includes but is not limited to, industrial, agricultural, or agro-industrial establishments engaged in the production, manufacturing, processing, repacking, or assembly of goods including service-oriented enterprises. v)   Skill refers to the acquired and practiced ability to carry out a task or job. vi) Skills Development refers to the process through which learners and workers are systematically provided with learning opportunities to acquire or upgrade, or both, their ability, knowledge, and behavior pattern required as qualifications for a job or range of jobs in a given occupational area. vii) Technical Education refers to the education process designed at upper secondary and lower tertiary levels, aligned with the levels of the PQF, with the pathways to higher education through the credit transfer system based on learning outcomes aimed at preparing technicians, technologists, para- professionals, and other categories of workers and/or entrepreneurs by providing them with a broad range of general education, theoretical, scientific and technological studies, and related job skills training. viii) Trade refers to any group of interrelated jobs or any occupation that is traditionally or officially recognized as craft or artisan in nature requiring specific qualifications that can be acquired through work experience and/or training; ix) Trainee refers to persons who are participants in a vocational, administrative, or technical training program for the purpose of acquiring and developing job-related skills; x)   Trainer refers to persons who direct the practice of skills towards immediate improvement in some task; xi) User-Led” or “Market-Driven Strategy refers to a strategy that promotes strengthened linkages between educational/training institutions and industry to ensure that appropriate skills and knowledge are provided by the educational system;

heading: Creation and Mandate of the Department of Technical Education and Skills
text: SEC. 5. Creation and Mandate of the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development. – There is hereby created a Department of Technical Education and Skills Development, hereinafter referred to as DTESD. The DTESD shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulatory, and administrative entity of the government for technical education and skills development programs. Page 6 of 15

heading: Powers and Functions
text: SEC. 6. Powers and Functions. – The DTESD shall have the following powers and functions: a) Formulate a roadmap for Philippine technical education and skills development and set the general directions for education and training policies and standards that shall be embodied in a National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan (NTESDP); b) Formulate and recommend national policies and guidelines and conduct in-depth studies on all policy areas and options that will promote technical education and skills development in consultation with the relevant stakeholders, and address job mismatch between technical vocational education and training and industry requirements; c) Assess, review, harmonize, and coordinate all technical education and skills development policies and programs to ensure overall relevance, consistency, responsiveness, effectiveness, and efficient implementation of the national policies; d) Organize and constitute various standing committees, subsidiary groups, or technical working groups for efficient integration, coordination, and monitoring of technical education and skills development programs at the national, regional, and local levels; e) Enter into, make, execute, perform, and carry out domestic and foreign contracts for the purpose of attaining its goals and objectives as provided for in this Act, subject to existing laws, rules, and regulations; f) Restructure the entire sub-sector consisting of all institutions and programs involved in the promotion and development of middle-level manpower through upgrading, merger, and/or phase-out following a user-led or market-driven strategy; g) Approve training standards and assessment packages as established, conducted, and proven effective by private industries; h) Establish and administer a system of accreditation of both public and private technical vocational institutions; i) Establish, develop, and support trainers’ training and/or programs; j) Impose reasonable fees and charges for such assessment and pieces of training conducted and retain such earnings for its own use, subject to guidelines that it shall promulgate and to government auditing rules and procedures; k) Allocate resources for the programs and projects it shall undertake pursuant to the approved NTESDP subject to pertinent laws, rules, and regulations; l) Determine and approve systematic funding schemes such as the levy and grant scheme for technical education and skills development purposes; m) Create, when deemed necessary, an Advisory Committee that shall provide expert and technical advice to the Secretary of the Department to be chosen from the academe and the private sector. Provided, That in case the Advisory Committee is created, the Department is authorized to set aside a portion of its appropriation for the Committee’s operations; Page 7 of 15 n) Formulate or review and recommend actions to concerned authorities on proposed technical assistance programs and grants-in-aid for technical education and skills development, including those which may be entered into between the Government and other nations, including international or foreign organizations whether doing business in the Philippines or not; o) Promulgate rules and regulations for the full, effective, and efficient implementation of its policies and related laws; and p) Perform such other functions as may be needed to achieve its goals and objectives to the fullest and as may be provided by this Act.

heading: Composition
text: SEC. 7. Composition. - The DTESD shall be composed of the Offices of the Department Secretary, the Undersecretaries, the Assistant Secretaries, and their immediate support staff. It shall also have bureaus, as well as regional and provincial or district offices. The Office of the Secretary shall be in the main office of the Department.

heading: Powers and Functions of the Secretary
text: SEC. 8. Powers and Functions of the Secretary. - The Secretary of the DTESD shall have the following functions: a) Provide executive direction and supervision over the entire operations of the DTESD; b) Organize the DTESD for the efficient and effective performance of its functions s o a s to achieve its goals and objectives under this Act; c) Represent and effectively advocate technical education and skills development (TESD) concerns in national and international bodies; d) Establish TESD policies and standards for the effective, efficient, and economical operation of the DTESD, consistent with and in accordance with the annual programs of the government; e) Mobilize resources and ensure prudent utilization of and access to TESD investments and incentives according to national development plans and priorities; f) Designate and appoint Regional Directors and other officers and employees of the DTESD, excluding the Undersecretaries and Assistant Secretaries, subject to and in accordance with Civil Service Laws, rules and regulations; g) Undertake consultations with other members of the Cabinet and officers of the government relating to TESD concerns; h) Advise the President on the promulgation of executive and administrative orders and formulation of regulatory and legislative proposals on matters pertaining to TESD; i)   Promulgate rules, regulations, and other issuances as may be necessary to carry out the DTESD’s mandate, objective, policies, plans, programs, goals, and projects; j)   Direct and manage the implementation of DTESD’s programs and services; and Page 8 of 15 k) Perform such other functions as may be authorized by law.

heading: Undersecretaries and Assistant Secretaries
text: SEC. 9. Undersecretaries and Assistant Secretaries. - The DTESD Secretary shall be assisted by three (3) Undersecretaries and three (3) Assistant Secretaries who shall be appointed by the President upon recommendation of the DTESD Secretary: Provided, that two (2) Undersecretaries and two (2) Assistant Secretaries shall be career officers. The Undersecretaries and Assistant Secretaries shall assist the Secretary in the performance of his powers and functions under this Act in order to fully achieve the goals and objectives of the DTESD. The Undersecretaries and Assistant Secretaries shall be given specific areas of responsibility by the Secretary.

heading: Qualifications and Appointments
text: SEC. 10. Qualifications and Appointments. – No Secretary, Undersecretary, or Assistant Secretary of the DTESD shall be appointed unless he/she is a natural-born Filipino citizen, a resident of the Philippines, of good moral character, of proven integrity, a college degree graduate, a Civil Service eligible or its equivalent, and with at least five (5) years of experience in technical education skills and development.

heading: Bureaus, Services, and Personnel
text: SEC. 11. Bureaus, Services, and Personnel. – The bureaus which shall be under the Office of the Secretary shall be headed by an Executive Director to be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the Secretary. The Executive Director shall have the rank and emoluments of Director IV and shall have the same qualifications as those of the Secretary, Undersecretary, and Assistant Secretary of the DTESD.

heading: Regional Office
text: SEC. 12. Regional Office – There shall be established a Regional Office in each region of the country to be headed by a Regional Director to be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the Secretary. A Regional Director shall have the rank and emoluments of Director IV and shall have the same qualifications as those of the Secretary, Undersecretary, and Assistant Secretary of the DTESD. The Regional Directors shall have the following functions: a)   Direct t h e implementation of TESD programs, projects, and related activities in the region; b)   Develop and recommend to the Secretary for approval TESD programs for local- level implementation within set policies; c)   Disseminate policies to stakeholders; d) Manage TESD resources in the region; e)   Plan and implement policy inputs in the region; f)   Monitor and evaluate program implementation; and g)   Perform such other functions as may be directed by the Secretary or as may be provided by law, rules or regulations, or executive issuances.

heading: The Provincial/District Offices
text: SEC. 13. The Provincial/District Offices.- The Provincial/District Office shall be headed Page 9 of 15 by a Provincial/District Director to be appointed by the Secretary of the DTESD. A Provincial/District Director shall have the rank and emoluments of Director III who shall be a natural-born Filipino citizen, a resident of the Province or District where he is appointed, of good moral character, of proven integrity, a college degree graduate, a Civil Service eligible, and with at least two (2) years of experience in technical education skills and development. A Provincial/District Director shall have the following functions: a)   Serve as secretariat to the Provincial Technical Education and Skills Development Committee; b)   Provide technical assistance to the local government units for effective supervision, coordination, and integration of all technical education and training programs within their localities; c)   Review and recommend to the Secretary priority technical education and training programs within their localities; and d) Perform such other functions as may be authorized or directed by the Secretary,

heading: Technical Education and Training Centers
text: SEC. 14. Technical Education and Training Centers. - The DTESD shall absorb and enhance existing government Technical Education and Training Centers, including the Cordillera State Institute of Technical Education or CSITE as provided under Republic Act No. 11192, and establish a network of national, regional, and local technical education and skills development centers for the purpose of promoting technical education and skills development. This network shall include leading training technology centers, training centers in vocational and technical schools, technical institutes, polytechnic colleges, and all other duly accredited public and private dual-system educational institutions. The technical education and skills development centers shall be administered and operated under such rules and regulations as may be established by the DTESD in accordance with the National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan. These centers and schools shall have the following functions: a)   Provide responsive formal and non-formal TESD programs; b)   Conduct applied research and development programs and provide extension services in coordination with Regional Offices (ROs)/Provincial Offices (POs); c)   Undertake entrepreneurship development program; d) Conduct outreach programs in coordination with ROs/POs; e)   Provide job linkages; f)   Provide assessment and certification; g)   Devise mechanisms for sustainable operation and development; h)   Monitor and evaluate program implementation; and Page 10 of 15 i)   Perform such other functions as may be authorized by law, rules, or regulations, including executive issuances.

heading: Structure and Staffing Pattern
text: SEC. 15. Structure and Staffing Pattern. - Subject to the approval of the DBM, the DTESD through the Office of the Secretary shall determine its organizational structure, staffing, pattern, qualification standards, and placement of personnel in the DTESD who shall be appointed in accordance with the civil service law, rules, and regulations.

heading: Compliance with the Salary Standardization Law
text: SEC. 16. Compliance with the Salary Standardization Law. - The compensation and emoluments of the officials and employees of the DTESD shall be in accordance with the salary standardization law and other applicable laws under the national compensation and clarification plan.

heading: Consultants and Technical Assistance, Publication and Research
text: SEC. 17. Consultants and Technical Assistance, Publication and Research. - In pursuance of its objectives, the DTESD is hereby authorized to set aside a portion of its appropriation for the hiring of services of qualified consultants, and private organizations for research work and publication in the field of technical education and training. It shall avail itself of the services of other agencies of the Government as may be necessary or required.

heading: Formulation of a Comprehensive Development Plan for Middle Level
text: SEC. 18. Formulation of a Comprehensive Development Plan for Middle Level Manpower. - The DTESD shall formulate a comprehensive development plan for middle manpower based on a national employment plan or policies for the optimum allocation, development, and utilization of skilled workers for employment, entrepreneurship, and technology development for economic and social growth. This plan shall be updated periodically and submitted to the President for approval. Thereafter, it shall be the plan for the technical education, training, and certification for the entire country within the framework of the National Development Plan. The DTESD may, through its various offices, call on public agencies, the private sector, and academe for assistance in the full and efficient implementation of this comprehensive plan. The comprehensive plan shall provide for a reformed industry-based training program including apprenticeship, dual training system, and other similar schemes intended to: a)   Promote maximum protection and welfare of the worker-trainee; b) Improve the quality, relevance, and social accountability of technical education and training; c)   Accelerate the employment generation effort of the government; and d) Expand the range of opportunities for upward social mobility of students beyond the traditional higher levels of formal education. All agencies receiving financial and technical assistance from the government shall be required to formulate their respective annual agency technical education and training plans and programs. The budget to support such plans and programs shall be subject to review and endorsement by the DTESD to the DBM. The DTESD shall evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of an agency’s skills development program and schemes to make them conform to the quantitative and qualitative objectives of the national technical Page 11 of 15 education and skills development plan.

heading: Technical Education and Skills Development Committees
text: SEC. 19. Technical Education and Skills Development Committees. - The DTESD shall establish Technical Education and Skills Development Committees for the regional and local development councils to coordinate and monitor the delivery of all training activities by the public and private sectors, and recommend policies, programs and projects to better carry out the objectives of this Act. The composition of these Committees shall be determined by the Secretary.

heading: Enterprise-Based Training Program
text: SEC. 20. Enterprise-Based Training Program. - The DTESD shall promote enterprise- based Training as the major mode of training rather than an employment arrangement and shall see to it that it is not subject to abuse by unscrupulous entities.

heading: Establishment and Administration of National Training Standards
text: SEC. 21. Establishment and Administration of National Training Standards. - There shall be national training standards to be established by DTESD-accredited industry committees. The DTESD shall develop and implement a certification and accreditation program in which private industry groups and trade associations are accredited to conduct approved assessment packages. The local government units shall promote these assessment packages in their respective areas in accordance with the guidelines set by the DTESD. The Secretary shall determine the occupational trades for mandatory certification. All certificates relating to the national training standards and certification system shall be issued by the DTESD through its Regional and Provincial Offices. In consonance with the Philippine Qualifications Framework (PQF), the DTESD shall closely collaborate with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) as regards the assessment of technicians, master craftsmen, and technologists.

heading: Administration of Training Programs
text: SEC. 22. Administration of Training Programs. - The DTESD shall design and administer training programs and schemes that will develop the capabilities of public and private institutions to provide quality and cost-effective technical education and skills development and related opportunities. Such training programs and schemes shall include teachers’/trainers’ training in occupational trades and related fields of employment and values development as an integral component of all technical education and training programs.

heading: Assistance to Employers and Organizations
text: SEC. 23. Assistance to Employers and Organizations. - The DTESD shall assist employers or organizations engaged in technical education and training schemes designed to attain its objectives under the rules and regulations established for the purpose.

heading: Accreditation and Regulation of Technical Education and Skills Development
text: SEC. 24. Accreditation and Regulation of Technical Education and Skills Development Programs. - All technical education and skills development programs shall be duly accredited by the DTESD before it is offered to the public by any public or private entity or non- government organization. Non-compliance with the accreditation requirements of the DTESD shall be a basis for the suspension or cancellation of the entity’s license to operate issued by competent authorities.

heading: Coordination of All Technical Education and Skills Development Schemes
text: SEC. 25. Coordination of All Technical Education and Skills Development Schemes. – In order to integrate the national technical education and skills development efforts, all Page 12 of 15 technical education and skills development programs and schemes as provided for in this Act shall comply with national standards as determined by the DTESD, particularly those having to do with competency standards. For this purpose, existing technical education and skills development programs in the Government and in the private sector, specifically those wholly or partly financed with government funds, shall be reported to the DTESD for assessment and evaluation to ensure their efficiency and effectiveness. Non-compliance with these standards including reportorial requirements shall be a disqualification from any form of government assistance in the field of technical education and skills development.

heading: Enterprise-based Partnerships and Linkages
text: SEC. 26. Enterprise-based Partnerships and Linkages. - The DTESD shall establish effective and efficient institutional arrangements with industry bodies and such other organizations or associations to ensure direct participation of employers and workers in the design and implementation of technical education and skills development schemes, competency standardization and certification, and such other functions in the fulfillment of the DTESD’s objectives.

heading: Inclusive Training Opportunities
text: SEC. 27. Inclusive Training Opportunities. - The DTESD shall likewise design and implement a delivery system for community- based technical education and skills development opportunities for the marginalized and disadvantaged sectors of the population, including the beneficiaries of Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) as provided under Republic Act No. 11310 or the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program Act, providing them with new tools of wealth creation and with the capability to take on higher value-added gainful activities, and to share equitably in productivity gains eventually leading to poverty alleviation and reduction.

heading: Skills Competitions
text: SEC. 28. Skills Competitions. - To promote quality technical education and skills development in the country and with the view of participating in international skills competitions, the DTESD, with the active participation of private industries, shall organize and conduct annual National Skills competitions. The DTESD shall promulgate the necessary rules and guidelines for the effective and efficient conduct of National Skills competitions and for the country’s participation in international Skills competitions such as ASEAN and World Skills Olympics.

heading: The TESD Development Fund
text: SEC. 29. The TESD Development Fund. - A Technical Education and Skills Development Fund is hereby established to be managed/administered by the DTESD, the income from which shall be utilized exclusively in awarding of grants and providing assistance to training institutions, industries, and local government units for upgrading their capabilities and to develop and implement skills development training and training-related activities. The contribution to the fund shall be the following: a) A one-time lump sum appropriation from the National Government; b) An annual contribution from the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration Fund, the amount of which shall be determined by the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration and based on the study on the financing capacity of the OWWA fund; c) Donations, grants, endowments, and other bequests or gifts, and any other income Page 13 of 15 generated by the DTESD. The Secretary shall be the administrator of the fund, and as such, shall formulate the necessary implementing guidelines for the management of the fund, subject to the following: a) Unless otherwise stipulated by the private donor, only earnings of private contributions shall be used; and b) No part of the seed capital of the fund, including earnings, thereof, shall be used to underwrite expenses for the administration of the Fund. The Secretary shall appoint a reputable government-accredited investment institution as the fund manager, subject to existing government rules and regulations.

heading: Technical Assistance, Incentives, and Scholarship Grants
text: SEC. 30. Technical Assistance, Incentives, and Scholarship Grants. - The DTESD shall adopt a system of providing technical assistance, incentives, and scholarship grants which shall be designed to encourage public and private sector and clientele participation in technical education and training activities along the priorities identified by the National Development Plan/Agenda.

heading: Placement Centers
text: SEC. 31. Placement Centers. - There shall be established a network of placement centers or PLACERS in all the Provincial/District Offices to cater specifically to the job placement of graduates of TESD institutions. These Centers shall be financed and administered by the DTESD. In coordination with the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), these centers shall be part of the National Employment Service Network of the DOLE.

heading: Separation and Retirement from Service
text: SEC. 32. Separation and Retirement from Service. - Employees who are separated from service within six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act as a result of the abolition/reorganization under the provisions of this Act shall receive separation benefits to which they may be entitled under existing laws, orders and issuances: Provided, that those who are qualified to retire under existing retirement laws shall be allowed to retire and receive retirement benefits to which they may be entitled under applicable laws, orders, and issuances.

heading: Transitory Provision
text: SEC. 33. Transitory Provision. – The Technical Education and Skills Development (TESDA) and the TESDA Board created under Republic Act No. 7796 are hereby abolished. The TESDA Secretariat created under Sections 10-15 of R.A. 7796 shall comprise the initial manpower complement of the DTESD, Provided, that, no employee shall be terminated by virtue of this transfer. The laws and rules on government reorganization as provided under Republic Act No. 6656, otherwise known as the Reorganization Law, shall govern the transfer and reorganization process of the DTESD. The personnel of the TESDA shall, in a holdover capacity, continue to perform their respective duties and responsibilities and receive their corresponding salaries and benefits until such time when the organizational structure pattern of the DTESD shall have been approved and implemented. Provided, That the preparation and approval of the new organizational structure and staffing pattern shall, as far as practicable, respect and ensure the security of tenure and seniority rights of affected employees. Those personnel whose positions are not included in the new staffing pattern or who are not reappointed or who choose to be separated as a result Page 14 of 15 of the reorganization shall be paid their separation and retirement benefits under existing laws.

heading: Appropriations
text: SEC. 34. Appropriations. - The amount needed for the initial implementation of this Act shall be taken from the current fiscal year’s appropriation of TESDA. Thereafter, the amount needed for the operation and maintenance of the DTESD shall be included in the General Appropriations Act.

heading: Implementing Rules and Regulations
text: SEC. 35. Implementing Rules and Regulations.- The DTESD, Department of Education, Department of Labor and Employment, Department of Budget and Management, and the Department of Finance shall, in consultation with other government agencies and concerned stakeholders, promulgate the implementing rules and regulations to effectively and efficiently carry out the provisions of this Act: Provided, That the non-promulgation of such rules and regulations shall not prevent the immediate implementation of this Act upon effectivity thereof.

heading: Separability Clause
text: SEC. 36. Separability Clause. - If, for any reason, any portion or provision of this Act shall be held unconstitutional or invalid, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.

heading: Repealing Clause
text: SEC. 37. Repealing Clause. - Republic Act No. 7796, otherwise known as the “TESDA Act of 1994,” is hereby repealed. All laws, presidential decrees, executive orders, rules and regulations, issuances, or parts thereof which are inconsistent with or contrary to the provisions of this Act are hereby deemed repealed, amended, or modified accordingly.

heading: Effectivity
text: SEC. 38. Effectivity. - This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation. Approved, Page 15 of 15

heading: Short Title
text: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Department of Technical Education Training and Certification (DepTeTC)."

heading: Declaration of Policy and Objectives
text: SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy and Objectives. — It is hereby declared the policy of the State to provide relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education, training and certification in support of the development of high-quality Filipino manpower responsive to and in accordance with Philippine development goals and priorities. The State shall encourage active participation of various concerned sectors, public as well as private tech-voc institutions particularly private enterprises, being direct participants in and immediate beneficiaries of a technically educated and trained workforces, in providing technical education services and training opportunities. It is the goal and objective of this Act to: a. Promote and strengthen the quality of technical education and training programs to attain global competitiveness. b. Focus technical education and training and certification on meeting the changing demands for quality manpower particularly in support of the industrialization thrust of the country; c. Encourage critical and creative thinking by disseminating the scientific and technical knowledge base of manpower development programs; 1 d. Recognize and encourage the complementary roles of public and private institutions in technical education and skills development and training systems; e. Inculcate desirable values through the development of moral character with emphasis on work ethic, self-discipline, self- reliance, and nationalism; f.   Strongly support the implementation of the Philippine Qualification Framework (E.O. 83 s. 2012), the Ladderized Education Program (RA 10647) and the Dual Technical Training System (R.A. 7686); g. Maximize returns to the country's investment in technical education and training through        an efficient graduates' employment facilitation program within the framework of the national employment service network system; and h. Help in the poverty alleviation efforts by providing the marginalized and vulnerable segments of the country's population access to income generating Technical Education and Training opportunities.

heading: Definition of Terms
text: SEC. 3. Definition of Terms. — As used in this Act: a. "Skill" shall mean the acquired and practiced ability to carry out a task or job; b. "Skills Development" shall mean the process through which learners and workers are systematically provided with learning opportunities to acquire or upgrade, or both, their ability, knowledge and behavior pattern required as qualifications for a job or range of jobs in a given occupational area. c. "Technical Education" shall refer to the education process designed at upper secondary and lower tertiary levels, aligned with the levels of the PQF, with the pathways to higher education through the credit transfer system based on learning outcomes aimed at preparing technicians, technologists, para-professionals and other categories of workers and/or entrepreneurs by providing them with a broad range of general education, theoretical, scientific and technological studies, and related job skills training. d. "Trade" shall mean any group of interrelated jobs or any occupation which is traditionally or officially recognized as craft or artisan in nature requiring specific qualifications that can be acquired through work experience and/or training. e. "Middle-Level Manpower" refers to those: 2 i.    who have acquired practical skills and knowledge through formal or non-formal education and training equivalent to at least a secondary education but preferably at post-secondary education with a corresponding degree of diploma; or ii.   skilled workers who have become highly competent in their trade or craft as attested by industry. f. Private Enterprises" refers to an economic system under which property of all kinds can be privately owned and in which individuals, alone or in association with another, can embark on a business activity. This includes industrial, agricultural, or agro- industrial establishments engaged in the production, manufacturing, processing, repacking or assembly of goods including service-oriented enterprises. g. "Trainers" shall mean persons who direct the practice of skills towards immediate improvement in some tasks. h. "Training" is teaching or developing oneself or others, any skills and knowledge that relate to specific useful competencies. i. "Trainors/trainers" shall mean persons who provide training to trainers aimed at developing the latter’s capacities for imparting attitudes, knowledge, skills and behavior patterns required for specific jobs, tasks, occupations or group of related occupations. j. Trainees" shall mean persons who are participants in a vocational, administrative or technical training program for the purpose of acquiring and developing job-related skills. k. "Apprenticeship" training within employment with compulsory related theoretical instruction involving a contract between an apprentice and an employer on an approved apprenticeable occupation. l. "Apprentice" is a person undergoing training for an approved apprenticeable occupation during an apprenticeship agreement. m. "Apprenticeship Agreement" is a contract wherein a prospective employer binds himself to train the apprentice who in tum accepts the terms of training for a recognized apprenticeable occupation emphasizing the rights, duties and responsibilities of each party. n. "Apprenticeable Occupation" is an occupation officially endorsed by a tripartite body and approved for apprenticeable by the Authority. 3 o. "Learners" refers to persons hired as trainees in semi-skilled and other industrial occupations which are non-apprenticeable. Learnership programs must be approved by the Authority. p. "User-Led" or "Market-Driven Strategy" refers to a strategy which promotes strengthened linkages between educational/training institutions and industry to ensure that appropriate skills and knowledge are provided by the educational system. q.
